---
name: webhook-subscriptions
description: Create and manage webhook subscriptions for event-driven agent activation, or for direct push notifications (zero LLM cost). Use when the user wants external services to trigger agent runs OR push notifications to chats.
version: 1.1.0
metadata:
  hermes:
    tags: [webhook, events, automation, integrations, notifications, push]
origin:
  source: hermes-agent
  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
  version: 9f22977f
---

# Webhook Subscriptions

Create dynamic webhook subscriptions so external services (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, CI/CD, IoT sensors, monitoring tools) can trigger Hermes agent runs by POSTing events to a URL.

## Setup (Required First)

The webhook platform must be enabled before subscriptions can be created. Check with:
```bash
hermes webhook list
```

If it says "Webhook platform is not enabled", set it up:

### Option 1: Setup wizard
```bash
hermes gateway setup
```
Follow the prompts to enable webhooks, set the port, and set a global HMAC secret.

### Option 2: Manual config
Add to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
platforms:
  webhook:
    enabled: true
    extra:
      host: "0.0.0.0"
      port: 8644
      secret: "generate-a-strong-secret-here"
```

### Option 3: Environment variables
Add to `~/.hermes/.env`:
```bash
WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true
WEBHOOK_PORT=8644
WEBHOOK_SECRET=generate-a-strong-secret-here
```

After configuration, start (or restart) the gateway:
```bash
hermes gateway run
# Or if using systemd:
systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway
```

Verify it's running:
```bash
curl http://localhost:8644/health
```

## Commands

All management is via the `hermes webhook` CLI command:

### Create a subscription
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe <name> \
  --prompt "Prompt template with {payload.fields}" \
  --events "event1,event2" \
  --description "What this does" \
  --skills "skill1,skill2" \
  --deliver telegram \
  --deliver-chat-id "12345" \
  --secret "optional-custom-secret"
```

Returns the webhook URL and HMAC secret. The user configures their service to POST to that URL.

### List subscriptions
```bash
hermes webhook list
```

### Remove a subscription
```bash
hermes webhook remove <name>
```

### Test a subscription
```bash
hermes webhook test <name>
hermes webhook test <name> --payload '{"key": "value"}'
```

## Prompt Templates

Prompts support `{dot.notation}` for accessing nested payload fields:

- `{issue.title}` — GitHub issue title
- `{pull_request.user.login}` — PR author
- `{data.object.amount}` — Stripe payment amount
- `{sensor.temperature}` — IoT sensor reading

If no prompt is specified, the full JSON payload is dumped into the agent prompt.

## Common Patterns

### GitHub: new issues
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe github-issues \
  --events "issues" \
  --prompt "New GitHub issue #{issue.number}: {issue.title}\n\nAction: {action}\nAuthor: {issue.user.login}\nBody:\n{issue.body}\n\nPlease triage this issue." \
  --deliver telegram \
  --deliver-chat-id "-100123456789"
```

Then in GitHub repo Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook:
- Payload URL: the returned webhook_url
- Content type: application/json
- Secret: the returned secret
- Events: "Issues"

### GitHub: PR reviews
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe github-prs \
  --events "pull_request" \
  --prompt "PR #{pull_request.number} {action}: {pull_request.title}\nBy: {pull_request.user.login}\nBranch: {pull_request.head.ref}\n\n{pull_request.body}" \
  --skills "github-code-review" \
  --deliver github_comment
```

### Stripe: payment events
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe stripe-payments \
  --events "payment_intent.succeeded,payment_intent.payment_failed" \
  --prompt "Payment {data.object.status}: {data.object.amount} cents from {data.object.receipt_email}" \
  --deliver telegram \
  --deliver-chat-id "-100123456789"
```

### CI/CD: build notifications
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe ci-builds \
  --events "pipeline" \
  --prompt "Build {object_attributes.status} on {project.name} branch {object_attributes.ref}\nCommit: {commit.message}" \
  --deliver discord \
  --deliver-chat-id "1234567890"
```

### Generic monitoring alert
```bash
hermes webhook subscribe alerts \
  --prompt "Alert: {alert.name}\nSeverity: {alert.severity}\nMessage: {alert.message}\n\nPlease investigate and suggest remediation." \
  --deliver origin
```

### Direct delivery (no agent, zero LLM cost)

For use cases where you just want to push a notification through to a user's chat — no reasoning, no agent loop — add `--deliver-only`. The rendered `--prompt` template becomes the literal message body and is dispatched directly to the target adapter.

Use this for:
- External service push notifications (Supabase/Firebase webhooks → Telegram)
- Monitoring alerts that should forward verbatim
- Inter-agent pings where one agent is telling another agent's user something
- Any webhook where an LLM round trip would be wasted effort

```bash
hermes webhook subscribe antenna-matches \
  --deliver telegram \
  --deliver-chat-id "123456789" \
  --deliver-only \
  --prompt "🎉 New match: {match.user_name} matched with you!" \
  --description "Antenna match notifications"
```

The POST returns `200 OK` on successful delivery, `502` on target failure — so upstream services can retry intelligently. HMAC auth, rate limits, and idempotency still apply.

Requires `--deliver` to be a real target (telegram, discord, slack, github_comment, etc.) — `--deliver log` is rejected because log-only direct delivery is pointless.

## Security

- Each subscription gets an auto-generated HMAC-SHA256 secret (or provide your own with `--secret`)
- The webhook adapter validates signatures on every incoming POST
- Static routes from config.yaml cannot be overwritten by dynamic subscriptions
- Subscriptions persist to `~/.hermes/webhook_subscriptions.json`

## How It Works

1. `hermes webhook subscribe` writes to `~/.hermes/webhook_subscriptions.json`
2. The webhook adapter hot-reloads this file on each incoming request (mtime-gated, negligible overhead)
3. When a POST arrives matching a route, the adapter formats the prompt and triggers an agent run
4. The agent's response is delivered to the configured target (Telegram, Discord, GitHub comment, etc.)

## Troubleshooting

If webhooks aren't working:

1. **Is the gateway running?** Check with `systemctl --user status hermes-gateway` or `ps aux | grep gateway`
2. **Is the webhook server listening?** `curl http://localhost:8644/health` should return `{"status": "ok"}`
3. **Check gateway logs:** `grep webhook ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log | tail -20`
4. **Signature mismatch?** Verify the secret in your service matches the one from `hermes webhook list`. GitHub sends `X-Hub-Signature-256`, GitLab sends `X-Gitlab-Token`.
5. **Firewall/NAT?** The webhook URL must be reachable from the service. For local development, use a tunnel (ngrok, cloudflared).
6. **Wrong event type?** Check `--events` filter matches what the service sends. Use `hermes webhook test <name>` to verify the route works.

Very thoroughly audit every SKILL.md file in crates/skills/src/assets/ to identify:

- HERMES_SPECIFIC — references Hermes internals
- HAS_REQUIRES — already declares requirements

    18→
    19→# Apple Reminders
    20→
    21→Use `remindctl` to manage Apple Reminders directly from the terminal. Tasks sync across all Apple devices via iCloud.
    22→
    23→## Prerequisites
    24→
    25→- **macOS** with Reminders.app
    26→- Install: `brew install steipete/tap/remindctl`
    27→- Grant Reminders permission when prompted
    28→- Check: `remindctl status` / Request: `remindctl authorize`
    29→
    30→## When to Use
    31→
    32→- User mentions "reminder" or "Reminders app"
    33→- Creating personal to-dos with due dates that sync to iOS
    34→- Managing Apple Reminders lists
    35→- User wants tasks to appear on their iPhone/iPad
    36→
    37→## When NOT to Use
    38→
    39→- Scheduling agent alerts → use the cronjob tool instead
    40→- Calendar events → use Apple Calendar or Google Calendar
    41→- Project task management → use GitHub Issues, Notion, etc.
    42→- If user says "remind me" but means an agent alert → clarify first
    43→
    44→## Quick Reference
    45→
    46→### View Reminders
    47→
    48→```bash
    49→remindctl                    # Today's reminders
    50→remindctl today              # Today
    51→remindctl tomorrow           # Tomorrow
    52→remindctl week               # This week
    53→remindctl overdue            # Past due
    54→remindctl all                # Everything
    55→remindctl 2026-01-04         # Specific date
    56→```
    57→
    58→### Manage Lists
    59→
    60→```bash
    61→remindctl list               # List all lists
    62→remindctl list Work          # Show specific list
    63→remindctl list Projects --create    # Create list
    64→remindctl list Work --delete        # Delete list
    65→```
    66→
    67→### Create Reminders
    68→
    69→```bash
    70→remindctl add "Buy milk"
    71→remindctl add --title "Call mom" --list Personal --due tomorrow
    72→remindctl add --title "Meeting prep" --due "2026-02-15 09:00"
    73→```
    74→
    75→### Complete / Delete
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→remindctl complete 1 2 3          # Complete by ID
    79→remindctl delete 4A83 --force     # Delete by ID
    80→```
    81→
    82→### Output Formats
    83→
    84→```bash
    85→remindctl today --json       # JSON for scripting
    86→remindctl today --plain      # TSV format
    87→remindctl today --quiet      # Counts only
    88→```
    89→
    90→## Date Formats
    91→
    92→Accepted by `--due` and date filters:
    93→- `today`, `tomorrow`, `yesterday`
    94→- `YYYY-MM-DD`
    95→- `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`
    96→- ISO 8601 (`2026-01-04T12:34:56Z`)
    97→
    98→## Rules
    99→
   100→1. When user says "remind me", clarify: Apple Reminders (syncs to phone) vs agent cronjob alert
   101→2. Always confirm reminder content and due date before creating
   102→3. Use `--json` for programmatic parsing
   103→

     4→version: 1.0.0

     7→platforms: [macos]
     8→metadata:
     9→  hermes:
    10→    tags: [FindMy, AirTag, location, tracking, macOS, Apple]

    13→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    14→  version: 9f22977f
    15→---
    16→
    17→# Find My (Apple)
    18→
    19→Track Apple devices and AirTags via the FindMy.app on macOS. Since Apple doesn't
    20→provide a CLI for FindMy, this skill uses AppleScript to open the app and
    21→screen capture to read device locations.
    22→
    23→## Prerequisites
    24→
    25→- **macOS** with Find My app and iCloud signed in
    26→- Devices/AirTags already registered in Find My
    27→- Screen Recording permission for terminal (System Settings → Privacy → Screen Recording)
    28→- **Optional but recommended**: Install `peekaboo` for better UI automation:
    29→  `brew install steipete/tap/peekaboo`
    30→
    31→## When to Use
    32→
    33→- User asks "where is my [device/cat/keys/bag]?"
    34→- Tracking AirTag locations
    35→- Checking device locations (iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods)
    36→- Monitoring pet or item movement over time (AirTag patrol routes)
    37→
    38→## Method 1: AppleScript + Screenshot (Basic)
    39→
    40→### Open FindMy and Navigate
    41→
    42→```bash
    43→# Open Find My app
    44→osascript -e 'tell application "FindMy" to activate'
    45→
    46→# Wait for it to load
    47→sleep 3
    48→
    49→# Take a screenshot of the Find My window
    50→screencapture -w -o /tmp/findmy.png
    51→```
    52→
    53→Then use `vision_analyze` to read the screenshot:
    54→```
    55→vision_analyze(image_url="/tmp/findmy.png", question="What devices/items are shown and what are their locations?")
    56→```
    57→
    58→### Switch Between Tabs
    59→
    60→```bash
    61→# Switch to Devices tab
    62→osascript -e '
    63→tell application "System Events"
    64→    tell process "FindMy"
    65→        click button "Devices" of toolbar 1 of window 1
    66→    end tell
    67→end tell'
    68→
    69→# Switch to Items tab (AirTags)
    70→osascript -e '
    71→tell application "System Events"
    72→    tell process "FindMy"
    73→        click button "Items" of toolbar 1 of window 1
    74→    end tell
    75→end tell'
    76→```
    77→
    78→## Method 2: Peekaboo UI Automation (Recommended)
    79→
    80→If `peekaboo` is installed, use it for more reliable UI interaction:
    81→
    82→```bash
    83→# Open Find My
    84→osascript -e 'tell application "FindMy" to activate'
    85→sleep 3
    86→
    87→# Capture and annotate the UI
    88→peekaboo see --app "FindMy" --annotate --path /tmp/findmy-ui.png
    89→
    90→# Click on a specific device/item by element ID
    91→peekaboo click --on B3 --app "FindMy"
    92→
    93→# Capture the detail view
    94→peekaboo image --app "FindMy" --path /tmp/findmy-detail.png
    95→```
    96→
    97→Then analyze with vision:
    98→```
    99→vision_analyze(image_url="/tmp/findmy-detail.png", question="What is the location shown for this device/item? Include address and coordinates if visible.")
   100→```
   101→
   102→## Workflow: Track AirTag Location Over Time
   103→
   104→For monitoring an AirTag (e.g., tracking a cat's patrol route):
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→# 1. Open FindMy to Items tab
   108→osascript -e 'tell application "FindMy" to activate'
   109→sleep 3
   110→
   111→# 2. Click on the AirTag item (stay on page — AirTag only updates when page is open)
   112→
   113→# 3. Periodically capture location
   114→while true; do
   115→    screencapture -w -o /tmp/findmy-$(date +%H%M%S).png
   116→    sleep 300  # Every 5 minutes
   117→done
   118→```
   119→
   120→Analyze each screenshot with vision to extract coordinates, then compile a route.
   121→
   122→## Limitations
   123→
   124→- FindMy has **no CLI or API** — must use UI automation
   125→- AirTags only update location while the FindMy page is actively displayed
   126→- Location accuracy depends on nearby Apple devices in the FindMy network
   127→- Screen Recording permission required for screenshots
   128→- AppleScript UI automation may break across macOS versions
   129→
   130→## Rules
   131→
   132→1. Keep FindMy app in the foreground when tracking AirTags (updates stop when minimized)
   133→2. Use `vision_analyze` to read screenshot content — don't try to parse pixels
   134→3. For ongoing tracking, use a cronjob to periodically capture and log locations
   135→4. Respect privacy — only track devices/items the user owns
   136→

    18→
    19→# iMessage
    20→
    21→Use `imsg` to read and send iMessage/SMS via macOS Messages.app.
    22→
    23→## Prerequisites
    24→
    25→- **macOS** with Messages.app signed in
    26→- Install: `brew install steipete/tap/imsg`
    27→- Grant Full Disk Access for terminal (System Settings → Privacy → Full Disk Access)
    28→- Grant Automation permission for Messages.app when prompted
    29→
    30→## When to Use
    31→
    32→- User asks to send an iMessage or text message
    33→- Reading iMessage conversation history
    34→- Checking recent Messages.app chats
    35→- Sending to phone numbers or Apple IDs
    36→
    37→## When NOT to Use
    38→
    39→- Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp messages → use the appropriate gateway channel
    40→- Group chat management (adding/removing members) → not supported
    41→- Bulk/mass messaging → always confirm with user first
    42→
    43→## Quick Reference
    44→
    45→### List Chats
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→imsg chats --limit 10 --json
    49→```
    50→
    51→### View History
    52→
    53→```bash
    54→# By chat ID
    55→imsg history --chat-id 1 --limit 20 --json
    56→
    57→# With attachments info
    58→imsg history --chat-id 1 --limit 20 --attachments --json
    59→```
    60→
    61→### Send Messages
    62→
    63→```bash
    64→# Text only
    65→imsg send --to "+14155551212" --text "Hello!"
    66→
    67→# With attachment
    68→imsg send --to "+14155551212" --text "Check this out" --file /path/to/image.jpg
    69→
    70→# Force iMessage or SMS
    71→imsg send --to "+14155551212" --text "Hi" --service imessage
    72→imsg send --to "+14155551212" --text "Hi" --service sms
    73→```
    74→
    75→### Watch for New Messages
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→imsg watch --chat-id 1 --attachments
    79→```
    80→
    81→## Service Options
    82→
    83→- `--service imessage` — Force iMessage (requires recipient has iMessage)
    84→- `--service sms` — Force SMS (green bubble)
    85→- `--service auto` — Let Messages.app decide (default)
    86→
    87→## Rules
    88→
    89→1. **Always confirm recipient and message content** before sending
    90→2. **Never send to unknown numbers** without explicit user approval
    91→3. **Verify file paths** exist before attaching
    92→4. **Don't spam** — rate-limit yourself
    93→
    94→## Example Workflow
    95→
    96→User: "Text mom that I'll be late"
    97→
    98→```bash
    99→# 1. Find mom's chat
   100→imsg chats --limit 20 --json | jq '.[] | select(.displayName | contains("Mom"))'
   101→
   102→# 2. Confirm with user: "Found Mom at +1555123456. Send 'I'll be late' via iMessage?"
   103→
   104→# 3. Send after confirmation
   105→imsg send --to "+1555123456" --text "I'll be late"
   106→```
   107→

     2→name: claude-code
     3→description: Delegate coding tasks to Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI agent). Use for building features, refactoring, PR reviews, and iterative coding. Requires the claude CLI installed.
     4→version: 2.2.0
     5→author: Hermes Agent + Teknium
     6→license: MIT
     7→metadata:
     8→  hermes:
     9→    tags: [Coding-Agent, Claude, Anthropic, Code-Review, Refactoring, PTY, Automation]
    10→    related_skills: [codex, hermes-agent, opencode]
    11→origin:
    12→  source: hermes-agent
    13→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    14→  version: 9f22977f
    15→---
    16→
    17→# Claude Code — Hermes Orchestration Guide
    18→
    19→Delegate coding tasks to [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) (Anthropic's autonomous coding agent CLI) via the Hermes terminal. Claude Code v2.x can read files, write code, run shell commands, spawn subagents, and manage git workflows autonomously.
    20→
    21→## Prerequisites
    22→
    23→- **Install:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`
    24→- **Auth:** run `claude` once to log in (browser OAuth for Pro/Max, or set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`)
    25→- **Console auth:** `claude auth login --console` for API key billing
    26→- **SSO auth:** `claude auth login --sso` for Enterprise
    27→- **Check status:** `claude auth status` (JSON) or `claude auth status --text` (human-readable)
    28→- **Health check:** `claude doctor` — checks auto-updater and installation health
    29→- **Version check:** `claude --version` (requires v2.x+)
    30→- **Update:** `claude update` or `claude upgrade`
    31→
    32→## Two Orchestration Modes
    33→
    34→Hermes interacts with Claude Code in two fundamentally different ways. Choose based on the task.
    35→
    36→### Mode 1: Print Mode (`-p`) — Non-Interactive (PREFERRED for most tasks)
    37→
    38→Print mode runs a one-shot task, returns the result, and exits. No PTY needed. No interactive prompts. This is the cleanest integration path.
    39→
    40→```
    41→terminal(command="claude -p 'Add error handling to all API calls in src/' --allowedTools 'Read,Edit' --max-turns 10", workdir="/path/to/project", timeout=120)
    42→```
    43→
    44→**When to use print mode:**
    45→- One-shot coding tasks (fix a bug, add a feature, refactor)
    46→- CI/CD automation and scripting
    47→- Structured data extraction with `--json-schema`
    48→- Piped input processing (`cat file | claude -p "analyze this"`)
    49→- Any task where you don't need multi-turn conversation
    50→
    51→**Print mode skips ALL interactive dialogs** — no workspace trust prompt, no permission confirmations. This makes it ideal for automation.
    52→
    53→### Mode 2: Interactive PTY via tmux — Multi-Turn Sessions
    54→
    55→Interactive mode gives you a full conversational REPL where you can send follow-up prompts, use slash commands, and watch Claude work in real time. **Requires tmux orchestration.**
    56→
    57→```
    58→# Start a tmux session
    59→terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s claude-work -x 140 -y 40")
    60→
    61→# Launch Claude Code inside it
    62→terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t claude-work 'cd /path/to/project && claude' Enter")
    63→
    64→# Wait for startup, then send your task
    65→# (after ~3-5 seconds for the welcome screen)
    66→terminal(command="sleep 5 && tmux send-keys -t claude-work 'Refactor the auth module to use JWT tokens' Enter")
    67→
    68→# Monitor progress by capturing the pane
    69→terminal(command="sleep 15 && tmux capture-pane -t claude-work -p -S -50")
    70→
    71→# Send follow-up tasks
    72→terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t claude-work 'Now add unit tests for the new JWT code' Enter")
    73→
    74→# Exit when done
    75→terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t claude-work '/exit' Enter")
    76→```
    77→
    78→**When to use interactive mode:**
    79→- Multi-turn iterative work (refactor → review → fix → test cycle)
    80→- Tasks requiring human-in-the-loop decisions
    81→- Exploratory coding sessions
    82→- When you need to use Claude's slash commands (`/compact`, `/review`, `/model`)
    83→
    84→## PTY Dialog Handling (CRITICAL for Interactive Mode)
    85→
    86→Claude Code presents up to two confirmation dialogs on first launch. You MUST handle these via tmux send-keys:
    87→
    88→### Dialog 1: Workspace Trust (first visit to a directory)
    89→```
    90→❯ 1. Yes, I trust this folder    ← DEFAULT (just press Enter)
    91→  2. No, exit
    92→```
    93→**Handling:** `tmux send-keys -t <session> Enter` — default selection is correct.
    94→
    95→### Dialog 2: Bypass Permissions Warning (only with --dangerously-skip-permissions)
    96→```
    97→❯ 1. No, exit                    ← DEFAULT (WRONG choice!)
    98→  2. Yes, I accept
    99→```
   100→**Handling:** Must navigate DOWN first, then Enter:
   101→```
   102→tmux send-keys -t <session> Down && sleep 0.3 && tmux send-keys -t <session> Enter
   103→```
   104→
   105→### Robust Dialog Handling Pattern
   106→```
   107→# Launch with permissions bypass
   108→terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t claude-work 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions \"your task\"' Enter")
   109→
   110→# Handle trust dialog (Enter for default "Yes")
   111→terminal(command="sleep 4 && tmux send-keys -t claude-work Enter")
   112→
   113→# Handle permissions dialog (Down then Enter for "Yes, I accept")
   114→terminal(command="sleep 3 && tmux send-keys -t claude-work Down && sleep 0.3 && tmux send-keys -t claude-work Enter")
   115→
   116→# Now wait for Claude to work
   117→terminal(command="sleep 15 && tmux capture-pane -t claude-work -p -S -60")
   118→```
   119→
   120→**Note:** After the first trust acceptance for a directory, the trust dialog won't appear again. Only the permissions dialog recurs each time you use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

   146→## Print Mode Deep Dive
   147→
   148→### Structured JSON Output
   149→```
   150→terminal(command="claude -p 'Analyze auth.py for security issues' --output-format json --max-turns 5", workdir="/project", timeout=120)
   151→```
   152→
   153→Returns a JSON object with:
   154→```json
   155→{
   156→  "type": "result",
   157→  "subtype": "success",
   158→  "result": "The analysis text...",
   159→  "session_id": "75e2167f-...",
   160→  "num_turns": 3,
   161→  "total_cost_usd": 0.0787,
   162→  "duration_ms": 10276,
   163→  "stop_reason": "end_turn",
   164→  "terminal_reason": "completed",
   165→  "usage": { "input_tokens": 5, "output_tokens": 603, ... },
   166→  "modelUsage": { "claude-sonnet-4-6": { "costUSD": 0.078, "contextWindow": 200000 } }
   167→}
   168→```
   169→
   170→**Key fields:** `session_id` for resumption, `num_turns` for agentic loop count, `total_cost_usd` for spend tracking, `subtype` for success/error detection (`success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_budget`).
   171→
   172→### Streaming JSON Output
   173→For real-time token streaming, use `stream-json` with `--verbose`:
   174→```
   175→terminal(command="claude -p 'Write a summary' --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages", timeout=60)
   176→```
   177→
   178→Returns newline-delimited JSON events. Filter with jq for live text:
   179→```
   180→claude -p "Explain X" --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages | \
   181→  jq -rj 'select(.type == "stream_event" and .event.delta.type? == "text_delta") | .event.delta.text'
   182→```
   183→
   184→Stream events include `system/api_retry` with `attempt`, `max_retries`, and `error` fields (e.g., `rate_limit`, `billing_error`).
   185→
   186→### Bidirectional Streaming
   187→For real-time input AND output streaming:
   188→```
   189→claude -p "task" --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --replay-user-messages
   190→```
   191→`--replay-user-messages` re-emits user messages on stdout for acknowledgment.
   192→
   193→### Piped Input
   194→```
   195→# Pipe a file for analysis
   196→terminal(command="cat src/auth.py | claude -p 'Review this code for bugs' --max-turns 1", timeout=60)
   197→
   198→# Pipe multiple files
   199→terminal(command="cat src/*.py | claude -p 'Find all TODO comments' --max-turns 1", timeout=60)
   200→
   201→# Pipe command output
   202→terminal(command="git diff HEAD~3 | claude -p 'Summarize these changes' --max-turns 1", timeout=60)
   203→```
   204→
   205→### JSON Schema for Structured Extraction
   206→```
   207→terminal(command="claude -p 'List all functions in src/' --output-format json --json-schema '{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"functions\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}},\"required\":[\"functions\"]}' --max-turns 5", workdir="/project", timeout=90)
   208→```
   209→
   210→Parse `structured_output` from the JSON result. Claude validates output against the schema before returning.
   211→
   212→### Session Continuation
   213→```
   214→# Start a task
   215→terminal(command="claude -p 'Start refactoring the database layer' --output-format json --max-turns 10 > /tmp/session.json", workdir="/project", timeout=180)
   216→
   217→# Resume with session ID
   218→terminal(command="claude -p 'Continue and add connection pooling' --resume $(cat /tmp/session.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"session_id\"])') --max-turns 5", workdir="/project", timeout=120)
   219→
   220→# Or resume the most recent session in the same directory
   221→terminal(command="claude -p 'What did you do last time?' --continue --max-turns 1", workdir="/project", timeout=30)
   222→
   223→# Fork a session (new ID, keeps history)
   224→terminal(command="claude -p 'Try a different approach' --resume <id> --fork-session --max-turns 10", workdir="/project", timeout=120)
   225→```
   226→
   227→### Bare Mode for CI/Scripting
   228→```
   229→terminal(command="claude --bare -p 'Run all tests and report failures' --allowedTools 'Read,Bash' --max-turns 10", workdir="/project", timeout=180)
   230→```
   231→
   232→`--bare` skips hooks, plugins, MCP discovery, and CLAUDE.md loading. Fastest startup. Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (skips OAuth).
   233→
   234→To selectively load context in bare mode:
   235→| To load | Flag |
   236→|---------|------|
   237→| System prompt additions | `--append-system-prompt "text"` or `--append-system-prompt-file path` |
   238→| Settings | `--settings <file-or-json>` |
   239→| MCP servers | `--mcp-config <file-or-json>` |
   240→| Custom agents | `--agents '<json>'` |
   241→
   242→### Fallback Model for Overload
   243→```
   244→terminal(command="claude -p 'task' --fallback-model haiku --max-turns 5", timeout=90)
   245→```
   246→Automatically falls back to the specified model when the default is overloaded (print mode only).

   248→## Complete CLI Flags Reference
   249→
   250→### Session & Environment
   251→| Flag | Effect |
   252→|------|--------|
   253→| `-p, --print` | Non-interactive one-shot mode (exits when done) |
   254→| `-c, --continue` | Resume most recent conversation in current directory |
   255→| `-r, --resume <id>` | Resume specific session by ID or name (interactive picker if no ID) |
   256→| `--fork-session` | When resuming, create new session ID instead of reusing original |
   257→| `--session-id <uuid>` | Use a specific UUID for the conversation |
   258→| `--no-session-persistence` | Don't save session to disk (print mode only) |
   259→| `--add-dir <paths...>` | Grant Claude access to additional working directories |
   260→| `-w, --worktree [name]` | Run in an isolated git worktree at `.claude/worktrees/<name>` |
   261→| `--tmux` | Create a tmux session for the worktree (requires `--worktree`) |
   262→| `--ide` | Auto-connect to a valid IDE on startup |
   263→| `--chrome` / `--no-chrome` | Enable/disable Chrome browser integration for web testing |
   264→| `--from-pr [number]` | Resume session linked to a specific GitHub PR |
   265→| `--file <specs...>` | File resources to download at startup (format: `file_id:relative_path`) |
   266→
   267→### Model & Performance
   268→| Flag | Effect |
   269→|------|--------|
   270→| `--model <alias>` | Model selection: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, or full name like `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
   271→| `--effort <level>` | Reasoning depth: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, `auto` | Both |
   272→| `--max-turns <n>` | Limit agentic loops (print mode only; prevents runaway) |
   273→| `--max-budget-usd <n>` | Cap API spend in dollars (print mode only) |
   274→| `--fallback-model <model>` | Auto-fallback when default model is overloaded (print mode only) |
   275→| `--betas <betas...>` | Beta headers to include in API requests (API key users only) |
   276→
   277→### Permission & Safety
   278→| Flag | Effect |
   279→|------|--------|
   280→| `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | Auto-approve ALL tool use (file writes, bash, network, etc.) |
   281→| `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` | Enable bypass as an *option* without enabling it by default |
   282→| `--permission-mode <mode>` | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions` |
   283→| `--allowedTools <tools...>` | Whitelist specific tools (comma or space-separated) |
   284→| `--disallowedTools <tools...>` | Blacklist specific tools |
   285→| `--tools <tools...>` | Override built-in tool set (`""` = none, `"default"` = all, or tool names) |
   286→
   287→### Output & Input Format
   288→| Flag | Effect |
   289→|------|--------|
   290→| `--output-format <fmt>` | `text` (default), `json` (single result object), `stream-json` (newline-delimited) |
   291→| `--input-format <fmt>` | `text` (default) or `stream-json` (real-time streaming input) |
   292→| `--json-schema <schema>` | Force structured JSON output matching a schema |
   293→| `--verbose` | Full turn-by-turn output |
   294→| `--include-partial-messages` | Include partial message chunks as they arrive (stream-json + print) |
   295→| `--replay-user-messages` | Re-emit user messages on stdout (stream-json bidirectional) |
   296→
   297→### System Prompt & Context
   298→| Flag | Effect |
   299→|------|--------|
   300→| `--append-system-prompt <text>` | **Add** to the default system prompt (preserves built-in capabilities) |
   301→| `--append-system-prompt-file <path>` | **Add** file contents to the default system prompt |
   302→| `--system-prompt <text>` | **Replace** the entire system prompt (use --append instead usually) |
   303→| `--system-prompt-file <path>` | **Replace** the system prompt with file contents |
   304→| `--bare` | Skip hooks, plugins, MCP discovery, CLAUDE.md, OAuth (fastest startup) |
   305→| `--agents '<json>'` | Define custom subagents dynamically as JSON |
   306→| `--mcp-config <path>` | Load MCP servers from JSON file (repeatable) |
   307→| `--strict-mcp-config` | Only use MCP servers from `--mcp-config`, ignoring all other MCP configs |
   308→| `--settings <file-or-json>` | Load additional settings from a JSON file or inline JSON |
   309→| `--setting-sources <sources>` | Comma-separated sources to load: `user`, `project`, `local` |
   310→| `--plugin-dir <paths...>` | Load plugins from directories for this session only |
   311→| `--disable-slash-commands` | Disable all skills/slash commands |
   312→
   313→### Debugging
   314→| Flag | Effect |
   315→|------|--------|
   316→| `-d, --debug [filter]` | Enable debug logging with optional category filter (e.g., `"api,hooks"`, `"!1p,!file"`) |
   317→| `--debug-file <path>` | Write debug logs to file (implicitly enables debug mode) |
   318→
   319→### Agent Teams
   320→| Flag | Effect |
   321→|------|--------|
   322→| `--teammate-mode <mode>` | How agent teams display: `auto`, `in-process`, or `tmux` |

   339→## Settings & Configuration
   340→
   341→### Settings Hierarchy (highest to lowest priority)
   342→1. **CLI flags** — override everything
   343→2. **Local project:** `.claude/settings.local.json` (personal, gitignored)
   344→3. **Project:** `.claude/settings.json` (shared, git-tracked)
   345→4. **User:** `~/.claude/settings.json` (global)
   346→
   347→### Permissions in Settings
   348→```json
   349→{
   350→  "permissions": {
   351→    "allow": ["Bash(npm run lint:*)", "WebSearch", "Read"],
   352→    "ask": ["Write(*.ts)", "Bash(git push*)"],
   353→    "deny": ["Read(.env)", "Bash(rm -rf *)"]
   354→  }
   355→}
   356→```

   358→### Memory Files (CLAUDE.md) Hierarchy
   359→1. **Global:** `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — applies to all projects
   360→2. **Project:** `./CLAUDE.md` — project-specific context (git-tracked)
   361→3. **Local:** `.claude/CLAUDE.local.md` — personal project overrides (gitignored)

   473→
   474→### Quick Review (Print Mode)
   475→```
   476→terminal(command="cd /path/to/repo && git diff main...feature-branch | claude -p 'Review this diff for bugs, security issues, and style problems. Be thorough.' --max-turns 1", timeout=60)
   477→```

   479→### Deep Review (Interactive + Worktree)
   480→```
   481→terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s review -x 140 -y 40")
   482→terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t review 'cd /path/to/repo && claude -w pr-review' Enter")
   483→terminal(command="sleep 5 && tmux send-keys -t review Enter")  # Trust dialog
   484→terminal(command="sleep 2 && tmux send-keys -t review 'Review all changes vs main. Check for bugs, security issues, race conditions, and missing tests.' Enter")
   485→terminal(command="sleep 30 && tmux capture-pane -t review -p -S -60")
   486→```

   488→### PR Review from Number
   489→```
   490→terminal(command="claude -p 'Review this PR thoroughly' --from-pr 42 --max-turns 10", workdir="/path/to/repo", timeout=120)
   491→```

   494→```
   495→terminal(command="claude -w feature-x --tmux", workdir="/path/to/repo")

   517→## CLAUDE.md — Project Context File
   518→
   519→Claude Code auto-loads `CLAUDE.md` from the project root. Use it to persist project context:
   520→
   521→```markdown
   522→# Project: My API
   523→
   524→## Architecture
   525→- FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy ORM
   526→- PostgreSQL database, Redis cache
   527→- pytest for testing with 90% coverage target
   528→
   529→## Key Commands
   530→- `make test` — run full test suite
   531→- `make lint` — ruff + mypy
   532→- `make dev` — start dev server on :8000
   533→
   534→## Code Standards
   535→- Type hints on all public functions
   536→- Docstrings in Google style
   537→- 2-space indentation for YAML, 4-space for Python
   538→- No wildcard imports
   539→```
   540→
   541→**Be specific.** Instead of "Write good code", use "Use 2-space indentation for JS" or "Name test files with `.test.ts` suffix." Specific instructions save correction cycles.
   542→
   543→### Rules Directory (Modular CLAUDE.md)
   544→For projects with many rules, use the rules directory instead of one massive CLAUDE.md:
   545→- **Project rules:** `.claude/rules/*.md` — team-shared, git-tracked
   546→- **User rules:** `~/.claude/rules/*.md` — personal, global
   547→
   548→Each `.md` file in the rules directory is loaded as additional context. This is cleaner than cramming everything into a single CLAUDE.md.
   549→
   550→### Auto-Memory
   551→Claude automatically stores learned project context in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`.
   552→- **Limit:** 25KB or 200 lines per project
   553→- This is separate from CLAUDE.md — it's Claude's own notes about the project, accumulated across sessions
   554→
   555→## Custom Subagents
   556→
   557→Define specialized agents in `.claude/agents/` (project), `~/.claude/agents/` (personal), or via `--agents` CLI flag (session):
   558→
   559→### Agent Location Priority
   560→1. `.claude/agents/` — project-level, team-shared
   561→2. `--agents` CLI flag — session-specific, dynamic
   562→3. `~/.claude/agents/` — user-level, personal
   563→
   564→### Creating an Agent
   565→```markdown
   566→# .claude/agents/security-reviewer.md
   567→---
   568→name: security-reviewer
   569→description: Security-focused code review
   570→model: opus
   571→tools: [Read, Bash]
   572→---
   573→You are a senior security engineer. Review code for:
   574→- Injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection)
   575→- Authentication/authorization flaws
   576→- Secrets in code
   577→- Unsafe deserialization
   578→```
   579→
   580→Invoke via: `@security-reviewer review the auth module`
   581→
   582→### Dynamic Agents via CLI
   583→```
   584→terminal(command="claude --agents '{\"reviewer\": {\"description\": \"Reviews code\", \"prompt\": \"You are a code reviewer focused on performance\"}}' -p 'Use @reviewer to check auth.py'", timeout=120)
   585→```
   586→
   587→Claude can orchestrate multiple agents: "Use @db-expert to optimize queries, then @security to audit the changes."
   588→
   589→## Hooks — Automation on Events
   590→
   591→Configure in `.claude/settings.json` (project) or `~/.claude/settings.json` (global):
   592→
   593→```json
   594→{
   595→  "hooks": {
   596→    "PostToolUse": [{
   597→      "matcher": "Write(*.py)",
   598→      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "ruff check --fix $CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS"}]
   599→    }],
   600→    "PreToolUse": [{
   601→      "matcher": "Bash",
   602→      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "if echo \"$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT\" | grep -q 'rm -rf'; then echo 'Blocked!' && exit 2; fi"}]
   603→    }],
   604→    "Stop": [{
   605→      "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "echo 'Claude finished a response' >> /tmp/claude-activity.log"}]
   606→    }]
   607→  }
   608→}
   609→```
   610→
   611→### All 8 Hook Types
   612→| Hook | When it fires | Common use |
   613→|------|--------------|------------|
   614→| `UserPromptSubmit` | Before Claude processes a user prompt | Input validation, logging |
   615→| `PreToolUse` | Before tool execution | Security gates, block dangerous commands (exit 2 = block) |
   616→| `PostToolUse` | After a tool finishes | Auto-format code, run linters |
   617→| `Notification` | On permission requests or input waits | Desktop notifications, alerts |
   618→| `Stop` | When Claude finishes a response | Completion logging, status updates |
   619→| `SubagentStop` | When a subagent completes | Agent orchestration |
   620→| `PreCompact` | Before context memory is cleared | Backup session transcripts |
   621→| `SessionStart` | When a session begins | Load dev context (e.g., `git status`) |
   622→
   623→### Hook Environment Variables
   624→| Variable | Content |
   625→|----------|---------|
   626→| `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` | Current project path |
   627→| `CLAUDE_FILE_PATHS` | Files being modified |
   628→| `CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT` | Tool parameters as JSON |
   629→
   630→### Security Hook Examples
   631→```json
   632→{
   633→  "PreToolUse": [{
   634→    "matcher": "Bash",
   635→    "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "if echo \"$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT\" | grep -qE 'rm -rf|git push.*--force|:(){ :|:& };:'; then echo 'Dangerous command blocked!' && exit 2; fi"}]
   636→  }]
   637→}
   638→```
   639→
   640→## MCP Integration
   641→
   642→Add external tool servers for databases, APIs, and services:
   643→
   644→```
   645→# GitHub integration
   646→terminal(command="claude mcp add -s user github -- npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-github", timeout=30)
   647→
   648→# PostgreSQL queries
   649→terminal(command="claude mcp add -s local postgres -- npx @anthropic-ai/server-postgres --connection-string postgresql://localhost/mydb", timeout=30)
   650→
   651→# Puppeteer for web testing
   652→terminal(command="claude mcp add puppeteer -- npx @anthropic-ai/server-puppeteer", timeout=30)
   653→```
   654→
   655→### MCP Scopes
   656→| Flag | Scope | Storage |
   657→|------|-------|---------|
   658→| `-s user` | Global (all projects) | `~/.claude.json` |
   659→| `-s local` | This project (personal) | `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) |
   660→| `-s project` | This project (team-shared) | `.claude/settings.json` (git-tracked) |
   661→
   662→### MCP in Print/CI Mode
   663→```
   664→terminal(command="claude --bare -p 'Query database' --mcp-config mcp-servers.json --strict-mcp-config", timeout=60)
   665→```
   666→`--strict-mcp-config` ignores all MCP servers except those from `--mcp-config`.
   667→
   668→Reference MCP resources in chat: `@github:issue://123`
   669→
   670→### MCP Limits & Tuning
   671→- **Tool descriptions:** 2KB cap per server for tool descriptions and server instructions
   672→- **Result size:** Default capped; use `maxResultSizeChars` annotation to allow up to **500K** characters for large outputs
   673→- **Output tokens:** `export MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=50000` — cap output from MCP servers to prevent context flooding
   674→- **Transports:** `stdio` (local process), `http` (remote), `sse` (server-sent events)
   675→
   676→## Monitoring Interactive Sessions
   677→
   678→### Reading the TUI Status
   679→```
   680→# Periodic capture to check if Claude is still working or waiting for input
   681→terminal(command="tmux capture-pane -t dev -p -S -10")
   682→```
   683→
   684→Look for these indicators:
   685→- `❯` at bottom = waiting for your input (Claude is done or asking a question)
   686→- `●` lines = Claude is actively using tools (reading, writing, running commands)
   687→- `⏵⏵ bypass permissions on` = status bar showing permissions mode
   688→- `◐ medium · /effort` = current effort level in status bar
   689→- `ctrl+o to expand` = tool output was truncated (can be expanded interactively)
   690→
   691→### Context Window Health
   692→Use `/context` in interactive mode to see a colored grid of context usage. Key thresholds:
   693→- **< 70%** — Normal operation, full precision
   694→- **70-85%** — Precision starts dropping, consider `/compact`
   695→- **> 85%** — Hallucination risk spikes significantly, use `/compact` or `/clear`
   696→
   697→## Environment Variables
   698→
   699→| Variable | Effect |
   700→|----------|--------|
   701→| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | API key for authentication (alternative to OAuth) |
   702→| `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` | Default effort: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, or `auto` |
   703→| `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` | Cap thinking tokens (set to `0` to disable thinking entirely) |
   704→| `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | Cap output from MCP servers (default varies; set e.g., `50000`) |
   705→| `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` | Enable alt-screen rendering to eliminate terminal flicker |
   706→| `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` | Strip credentials from sub-processes for security |
   707→
   708→## Cost & Performance Tips
   709→
   710→1. **Use `--max-turns`** in print mode to prevent runaway loops. Start with 5-10 for most tasks.
   711→2. **Use `--max-budget-usd`** for cost caps. Note: minimum ~$0.05 for system prompt cache creation.
   712→3. **Use `--effort low`** for simple tasks (faster, cheaper). `high` or `max` for complex reasoning.
   713→4. **Use `--bare`** for CI/scripting to skip plugin/hook discovery overhead.
   714→5. **Use `--allowedTools`** to restrict to only what's needed (e.g., `Read` only for reviews).
   715→6. **Use `/compact`** in interactive sessions when context gets large.
   716→7. **Pipe input** instead of having Claude read files when you just need analysis of known content.
   717→8. **Use `--model haiku`** for simple tasks (cheaper) and `--model opus` for complex multi-step work.
   718→9. **Use `--fallback-model haiku`** in print mode to gracefully handle model overload.
   719→10. **Start new sessions for distinct tasks** — sessions last 5 hours; fresh context is more efficient.
   720→11. **Use `--no-session-persistence`** in CI to avoid accumulating saved sessions on disk.
   721→
   722→## Pitfalls & Gotchas
   723→
   724→1. **Interactive mode REQUIRES tmux** — Claude Code is a full TUI app. Using `pty=true` alone in Hermes terminal works but tmux gives you `capture-pane` for monitoring and `send-keys` for input, which is essential for orchestration.
   725→2. **`--dangerously-skip-permissions` dialog defaults to "No, exit"** — you must send Down then Enter to accept. Print mode (`-p`) skips this entirely.
   726→3. **`--max-budget-usd` minimum is ~$0.05** — system prompt cache creation alone costs this much. Setting lower will error immediately.
   727→4. **`--max-turns` is print-mode only** — ignored in interactive sessions.
   728→5. **Claude may use `python` instead of `python3`** — on systems without a `python` symlink, Claude's bash commands will fail on first try but it self-corrects.
   729→6. **Session resumption requires same directory** — `--continue` finds the most recent session for the current working directory.
   730→7. **`--json-schema` needs enough `--max-turns`** — Claude must read files before producing structured output, which takes multiple turns.
   731→8. **Trust dialog only appears once per directory** — first-time only, then cached.
   732→9. **Background tmux sessions persist** — always clean up with `tmux kill-session -t <name>` when done.
   733→10. **Slash commands (like `/commit`) only work in interactive mode** — in `-p` mode, describe the task in natural language instead.
   734→11. **`--bare` skips OAuth** — requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var or an `apiKeyHelper` in settings.
   735→12. **Context degradation is real** — AI output quality measurably degrades above 70% context window usage. Monitor with `/context` and proactively `/compact`.
   736→
   737→## Rules for Hermes Agents
   738→
   739→1. **Prefer print mode (`-p`) for single tasks** — cleaner, no dialog handling, structured output
   740→2. **Use tmux for multi-turn interactive work** — the only reliable way to orchestrate the TUI
   741→3. **Always set `workdir`** — keep Claude focused on the right project directory
   742→4. **Set `--max-turns` in print mode** — prevents infinite loops and runaway costs
   743→5. **Monitor tmux sessions** — use `tmux capture-pane -t <session> -p -S -50` to check progress
   744→6. **Look for the `❯` prompt** — indicates Claude is waiting for input (done or asking a question)
   745→7. **Clean up tmux sessions** — kill them when done to avoid resource leaks
   746→8. **Report results to user** — after completion, summarize what Claude did and what changed
   747→9. **Don't kill slow sessions** — Claude may be doing multi-step work; check progress instead
   748→10. **Use `--allowedTools`** — restrict capabilities to what the task actually needs
   749→

    16→
    17→# Codex CLI
    18→
    19→Delegate coding tasks to [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) via the Hermes terminal. Codex is OpenAI's autonomous coding agent CLI.
    20→
    21→## Prerequisites
    22→
    23→- Codex installed: `npm install -g @openai/codex`
    24→- OpenAI API key configured
    25→- **Must run inside a git repository** — Codex refuses to run outside one
    26→- Use `pty=true` in terminal calls — Codex is an interactive terminal app
    27→
    28→## One-Shot Tasks
    29→
    30→```
    31→terminal(command="codex exec 'Add dark mode toggle to settings'", workdir="~/project", pty=true)
    32→```
    33→
    34→For scratch work (Codex needs a git repo):
    35→```
    36→terminal(command="cd $(mktemp -d) && git init && codex exec 'Build a snake game in Python'", pty=true)
    37→```
    38→
    39→## Background Mode (Long Tasks)
    40→
    41→```
    42→# Start in background with PTY
    43→terminal(command="codex exec --full-auto 'Refactor the auth module'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
    44→# Returns session_id
    45→
    46→# Monitor progress
    47→process(action="poll", session_id="<id>")
    48→process(action="log", session_id="<id>")
    49→
    50→# Send input if Codex asks a question
    51→process(action="submit", session_id="<id>", data="yes")
    52→
    53→# Kill if needed
    54→process(action="kill", session_id="<id>")
    55→```
    56→
    57→## Key Flags
    58→
    59→| Flag | Effect |
    60→|------|--------|
    61→| `exec "prompt"` | One-shot execution, exits when done |
    62→| `--full-auto` | Sandboxed but auto-approves file changes in workspace |
    63→| `--yolo` | No sandbox, no approvals (fastest, most dangerous) |
    64→
    65→## PR Reviews
    66→
    67→Clone to a temp directory for safe review:
    68→
    69→```
    70→terminal(command="REVIEW=$(mktemp -d) && git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git $REVIEW && cd $REVIEW && gh pr checkout 42 && codex review --base origin/main", pty=true)
    71→```
    72→
    73→## Parallel Issue Fixing with Worktrees
    74→
    75→```
    76→# Create worktrees
    77→terminal(command="git worktree add -b fix/issue-78 /tmp/issue-78 main", workdir="~/project")
    78→terminal(command="git worktree add -b fix/issue-99 /tmp/issue-99 main", workdir="~/project")
    79→
    80→# Launch Codex in each
    81→terminal(command="codex --yolo exec 'Fix issue #78: <description>. Commit when done.'", workdir="/tmp/issue-78", background=true, pty=true)
    82→terminal(command="codex --yolo exec 'Fix issue #99: <description>. Commit when done.'", workdir="/tmp/issue-99", background=true, pty=true)
    83→
    84→# Monitor
    85→process(action="list")
    86→
    87→# After completion, push and create PRs
    88→terminal(command="cd /tmp/issue-78 && git push -u origin fix/issue-78")
    89→terminal(command="gh pr create --repo user/repo --head fix/issue-78 --title 'fix: ...' --body '...'")
    90→
    91→# Cleanup
    92→terminal(command="git worktree remove /tmp/issue-78", workdir="~/project")
    93→```
    94→
    95→## Batch PR Reviews
    96→
    97→```
    98→# Fetch all PR refs
    99→terminal(command="git fetch origin '+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/*'", workdir="~/project")
   100→
   101→# Review multiple PRs in parallel
   102→terminal(command="codex exec 'Review PR #86. git diff origin/main...origin/pr/86'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
   103→terminal(command="codex exec 'Review PR #87. git diff origin/main...origin/pr/87'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
   104→
   105→# Post results
   106→terminal(command="gh pr comment 86 --body '<review>'", workdir="~/project")
   107→```
   108→
   109→## Rules
   110→
   111→1. **Always use `pty=true`** — Codex is an interactive terminal app and hangs without a PTY
   112→2. **Git repo required** — Codex won't run outside a git directory. Use `mktemp -d && git init` for scratch
   113→3. **Use `exec` for one-shots** — `codex exec "prompt"` runs and exits cleanly
   114→4. **`--full-auto` for building** — auto-approves changes within the sandbox
   115→5. **Background for long tasks** — use `background=true` and monitor with `process` tool
   116→6. **Don't interfere** — monitor with `poll`/`log`, be patient with long-running tasks
   117→7. **Parallel is fine** — run multiple Codex processes at once for batch work
   118→

     2→name: opencode
     3→description: Delegate coding tasks to OpenCode CLI agent for feature implementation, refactoring, PR review, and long-running autonomous sessions. Requires the opencode CLI installed and authenticated.
     4→version: 1.2.0
     5→author: Hermes Agent
     6→license: MIT
     7→metadata:
     8→  hermes:
     9→    tags: [Coding-Agent, OpenCode, Autonomous, Refactoring, Code-Review]
    10→    related_skills: [claude-code, codex, hermes-agent]
    11→origin:
    12→  source: hermes-agent
    13→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    14→  version: 9f22977f
    15→---
    16→
    17→# OpenCode CLI
    18→
    19→Use [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) as an autonomous coding worker orchestrated by Hermes terminal/process tools. OpenCode is a provider-agnostic, open-source AI coding agent with a TUI and CLI.
    20→
    21→## When to Use
    22→
    23→- User explicitly asks to use OpenCode
    24→- You want an external coding agent to implement/refactor/review code
    25→- You need long-running coding sessions with progress checks
    26→- You want parallel task execution in isolated workdirs/worktrees
    27→
    28→## Prerequisites
    29→
    30→- OpenCode installed: `npm i -g opencode-ai@latest` or `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode`
    31→- Auth configured: `opencode auth login` or set provider env vars (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, etc.)
    32→- Verify: `opencode auth list` should show at least one provider
    33→- Git repository for code tasks (recommended)
    34→- `pty=true` for interactive TUI sessions
    35→
    36→## Binary Resolution (Important)
    37→
    38→Shell environments may resolve different OpenCode binaries. If behavior differs between your terminal and Hermes, check:
    39→
    40→```
    41→terminal(command="which -a opencode")
    42→terminal(command="opencode --version")
    43→```
    44→
    45→If needed, pin an explicit binary path:
    46→
    47→```
    48→terminal(command="$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode run '...'", workdir="~/project", pty=true)
    49→```
    50→
    51→## One-Shot Tasks
    52→
    53→Use `opencode run` for bounded, non-interactive tasks:
    54→
    55→```
    56→terminal(command="opencode run 'Add retry logic to API calls and update tests'", workdir="~/project")
    57→```
    58→
    59→Attach context files with `-f`:
    60→
    61→```
    62→terminal(command="opencode run 'Review this config for security issues' -f config.yaml -f .env.example", workdir="~/project")
    63→```
    64→
    65→Show model thinking with `--thinking`:
    66→
    67→```
    68→terminal(command="opencode run 'Debug why tests fail in CI' --thinking", workdir="~/project")
    69→```
    70→
    71→Force a specific model:
    72→
    73→```
    74→terminal(command="opencode run 'Refactor auth module' --model openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4", workdir="~/project")
    75→```
    76→
    77→## Interactive Sessions (Background)
    78→
    79→For iterative work requiring multiple exchanges, start the TUI in background:
    80→
    81→```
    82→terminal(command="opencode", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
    83→# Returns session_id
    84→
    85→# Send a prompt
    86→process(action="submit", session_id="<id>", data="Implement OAuth refresh flow and add tests")
    87→
    88→# Monitor progress
    89→process(action="poll", session_id="<id>")
    90→process(action="log", session_id="<id>")
    91→
    92→# Send follow-up input
    93→process(action="submit", session_id="<id>", data="Now add error handling for token expiry")
    94→
    95→# Exit cleanly — Ctrl+C
    96→process(action="write", session_id="<id>", data="\x03")
    97→# Or just kill the process
    98→process(action="kill", session_id="<id>")
    99→```
   100→
   101→**Important:** Do NOT use `/exit` — it is not a valid OpenCode command and will open an agent selector dialog instead. Use Ctrl+C (`\x03`) or `process(action="kill")` to exit.
   102→
   103→### TUI Keybindings
   104→
   105→| Key | Action |
   106→|-----|--------|
   107→| `Enter` | Submit message (press twice if needed) |
   108→| `Tab` | Switch between agents (build/plan) |
   109→| `Ctrl+P` | Open command palette |
   110→| `Ctrl+X L` | Switch session |
   111→| `Ctrl+X M` | Switch model |
   112→| `Ctrl+X N` | New session |
   113→| `Ctrl+X E` | Open editor |
   114→| `Ctrl+C` | Exit OpenCode |
   115→
   116→### Resuming Sessions
   117→
   118→After exiting, OpenCode prints a session ID. Resume with:
   119→
   120→```
   121→terminal(command="opencode -c", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)  # Continue last session
   122→terminal(command="opencode -s ses_abc123", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)  # Specific session
   123→```
   124→
   125→## Common Flags
   126→
   127→| Flag | Use |
   128→|------|-----|
   129→| `run 'prompt'` | One-shot execution and exit |
   130→| `--continue` / `-c` | Continue the last OpenCode session |
   131→| `--session <id>` / `-s` | Continue a specific session |
   132→| `--agent <name>` | Choose OpenCode agent (build or plan) |
   133→| `--model provider/model` | Force specific model |
   134→| `--format json` | Machine-readable output/events |
   135→| `--file <path>` / `-f` | Attach file(s) to the message |
   136→| `--thinking` | Show model thinking blocks |
   137→| `--variant <level>` | Reasoning effort (high, max, minimal) |
   138→| `--title <name>` | Name the session |
   139→| `--attach <url>` | Connect to a running opencode server |
   140→
   141→## Procedure
   142→
   143→1. Verify tool readiness:
   144→   - `terminal(command="opencode --version")`
   145→   - `terminal(command="opencode auth list")`
   146→2. For bounded tasks, use `opencode run '...'` (no pty needed).
   147→3. For iterative tasks, start `opencode` with `background=true, pty=true`.
   148→4. Monitor long tasks with `process(action="poll"|"log")`.
   149→5. If OpenCode asks for input, respond via `process(action="submit", ...)`.
   150→6. Exit with `process(action="write", data="\x03")` or `process(action="kill")`.
   151→7. Summarize file changes, test results, and next steps back to user.
   152→
   153→## PR Review Workflow
   154→
   155→OpenCode has a built-in PR command:
   156→
   157→```
   158→terminal(command="opencode pr 42", workdir="~/project", pty=true)
   159→```
   160→
   161→Or review in a temporary clone for isolation:
   162→
   163→```
   164→terminal(command="REVIEW=$(mktemp -d) && git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git $REVIEW && cd $REVIEW && opencode run 'Review this PR vs main. Report bugs, security risks, test gaps, and style issues.' -f $(git diff origin/main --name-only | head -20 | tr '\n' ' ')", pty=true)
   165→```
   166→
   167→## Parallel Work Pattern
   168→
   169→Use separate workdirs/worktrees to avoid collisions:
   170→
   171→```
   172→terminal(command="opencode run 'Fix issue #101 and commit'", workdir="/tmp/issue-101", background=true, pty=true)
   173→terminal(command="opencode run 'Add parser regression tests and commit'", workdir="/tmp/issue-102", background=true, pty=true)
   174→process(action="list")
   175→```
   176→
   177→## Session & Cost Management
   178→
   179→List past sessions:
   180→
   181→```
   182→terminal(command="opencode session list")
   183→```
   184→
   185→Check token usage and costs:
   186→
   187→```
   188→terminal(command="opencode stats")
   189→terminal(command="opencode stats --days 7 --models anthropic/claude-sonnet-4")
   190→```
   191→
   192→## Pitfalls
   193→
   194→- Interactive `opencode` (TUI) sessions require `pty=true`. The `opencode run` command does NOT need pty.
   195→- `/exit` is NOT a valid command — it opens an agent selector. Use Ctrl+C to exit the TUI.
   196→- PATH mismatch can select the wrong OpenCode binary/model config.
   197→- If OpenCode appears stuck, inspect logs before killing:
   198→  - `process(action="log", session_id="<id>")`
   199→- Avoid sharing one working directory across parallel OpenCode sessions.
   200→- Enter may need to be pressed twice to submit in the TUI (once to finalize text, once to send).
   201→
   202→## Verification
   203→
   204→Smoke test:
   205→
   206→```
   207→terminal(command="opencode run 'Respond with exactly: OPENCODE_SMOKE_OK'")
   208→```
   209→
   210→Success criteria:
   211→- Output includes `OPENCODE_SMOKE_OK`
   212→- Command exits without provider/model errors
   213→- For code tasks: expected files changed and tests pass
   214→
   215→## Rules
   216→
   217→1. Prefer `opencode run` for one-shot automation — it's simpler and doesn't need pty.
   218→2. Use interactive background mode only when iteration is needed.
   219→3. Always scope OpenCode sessions to a single repo/workdir.
   220→4. For long tasks, provide progress updates from `process` logs.
   221→5. Report concrete outcomes (files changed, tests, remaining risks).

Covers: video-to-ASCII conversion, audio-reactive music visualizers, generative ASCII art animations, hybrid video+audio reactive, text/lyrics overlays, real-time terminal rendering. Use when users request: ASCII video, text art video, terminal-style video, character art animation, retro text visualization, audio visualizer in ASCII, converting video to ASCII art, matrix-style effects, or any animated ASCII output."

     8→---
     9→
    10→# ASCII Video Production Pipeline
    11→
    12→## Creative Standard
    13→
    14→This is visual art. ASCII characters are the medium; cinema is the standard.
    15→
    16→**Before writing a single line of code**, articulate the creative concept. What is the mood? What visual story does this tell? What makes THIS project different from every other ASCII video? The user's prompt is a starting point — interpret it with creative ambition, not literal transcription.
    17→
    18→**First-render excellence is non-negotiable.** The output must be visually striking without requiring revision rounds. If something looks generic, flat, or like "AI-generated ASCII art," it is wrong — rethink the creative concept before shipping.
    19→
    20→**Go beyond the reference vocabulary.** The effect catalogs, shader presets, and palette libraries in the references are a starting vocabulary. For every project, combine, modify, and invent new patterns. The catalog is a palette of paints — you write the painting.
    21→
    22→**Be proactively creative.** Extend the skill's vocabulary when the project calls for it. If the references don't have what the vision demands, build it. Include at least one visual moment the user didn't ask for but will appreciate — a transition, an effect, a color choice that elevates the whole piece.
    23→
    24→**Cohesive aesthetic over technical correctness.** All scenes in a video must feel connected by a unifying visual language — shared color temperature, related character palettes, consistent motion vocabulary. A technically correct video where every scene uses a random different effect is an aesthetic failure.
    25→
    26→**Dense, layered, considered.** Every frame should reward viewing. Never flat black backgrounds. Always multi-grid composition. Always per-scene variation. Always intentional color.
    27→
    28→## Modes
    29→
    30→| Mode | Input | Output | Reference |
    31→|------|-------|--------|-----------|
    32→| **Video-to-ASCII** | Video file | ASCII recreation of source footage | `references/inputs.md` § Video Sampling |
    33→| **Audio-reactive** | Audio file | Generative visuals driven by audio features | `references/inputs.md` § Audio Analysis |
    34→| **Generative** | None (or seed params) | Procedural ASCII animation | `references/effects.md` |
    35→| **Hybrid** | Video + audio | ASCII video with audio-reactive overlays | Both input refs |
    36→| **Lyrics/text** | Audio + text/SRT | Timed text with visual effects | `references/inputs.md` § Text/Lyrics |
    37→| **TTS narration** | Text quotes + TTS API | Narrated testimonial/quote video with typed text | `references/inputs.md` § TTS Integration |
    38→
    39→## Stack
    40→
    41→Single self-contained Python script per project. No GPU required.
    42→
    43→| Layer | Tool | Purpose |
    44→|-------|------|---------|
    45→| Core | Python 3.10+, NumPy | Math, array ops, vectorized effects |
    46→| Signal | SciPy | FFT, peak detection (audio modes) |
    47→| Imaging | Pillow (PIL) | Font rasterization, frame decoding, image I/O |
    48→| Video I/O | ffmpeg (CLI) | Decode input, encode output, mux audio |
    49→| Parallel | concurrent.futures | N workers for batch/clip rendering |
    50→| TTS | ElevenLabs API (optional) | Generate narration clips |
    51→| Optional | OpenCV | Video frame sampling, edge detection |
    52→
    53→## Pipeline Architecture
    54→
    55→Every mode follows the same 6-stage pipeline:
    56→
    57→```
    58→INPUT → ANALYZE → SCENE_FN → TONEMAP → SHADE → ENCODE
    59→```
    60→
    61→1. **INPUT** — Load/decode source material (video frames, audio samples, images, or nothing)
    62→2. **ANALYZE** — Extract per-frame features (audio bands, video luminance/edges, motion vectors)
    63→3. **SCENE_FN** — Scene function renders to pixel canvas (`uint8 H,W,3`). Composes multiple character grids via `_render_vf()` + pixel blend modes. See `references/composition.md`
    64→4. **TONEMAP** — Percentile-based adaptive brightness normalization. See `references/composition.md` § Adaptive Tonemap
    65→5. **SHADE** — Post-processing via `ShaderChain` + `FeedbackBuffer`. See `references/shaders.md`
    66→6. **ENCODE** — Pipe raw RGB frames to ffmpeg for H.264/GIF encoding
    67→
    68→## Creative Direction
    69→
    70→### Aesthetic Dimensions
    71→
    72→| Dimension | Options | Reference |
    73→|-----------|---------|-----------|
    74→| **Character palette** | Density ramps, block elements, symbols, scripts (katakana, Greek, runes, braille), project-specific | `architecture.md` § Palettes |
    75→| **Color strategy** | HSV, OKLAB/OKLCH, discrete RGB palettes, auto-generated harmony, monochrome, temperature | `architecture.md` § Color System |
    76→| **Background texture** | Sine fields, fBM noise, domain warp, voronoi, reaction-diffusion, cellular automata, video | `effects.md` |
    77→| **Primary effects** | Rings, spirals, tunnel, vortex, waves, interference, aurora, fire, SDFs, strange attractors | `effects.md` |
    78→| **Particles** | Sparks, snow, rain, bubbles, runes, orbits, flocking boids, flow-field followers, trails | `effects.md` § Particles |
    79→| **Shader mood** | Retro CRT, clean modern, glitch art, cinematic, dreamy, industrial, psychedelic | `shaders.md` |
    80→| **Grid density** | xs(8px) through xxl(40px), mixed per layer | `architecture.md` § Grid System |
    81→| **Coordinate space** | Cartesian, polar, tiled, rotated, fisheye, Möbius, domain-warped | `effects.md` § Transforms |
    82→| **Feedback** | Zoom tunnel, rainbow trails, ghostly echo, rotating mandala, color evolution | `composition.md` § Feedback |
    83→| **Masking** | Circle, ring, gradient, text stencil, animated iris/wipe/dissolve | `composition.md` § Masking |
    84→| **Transitions** | Crossfade, wipe, dissolve, glitch cut, iris, mask-based reveal | `shaders.md` § Transitions |
    85→
    86→### Per-Section Variation
    87→
    88→Never use the same config for the entire video. For each section/scene:
    89→- **Different background effect** (or compose 2-3)
    90→- **Different character palette** (match the mood)
    91→- **Different color strategy** (or at minimum a different hue)
    92→- **Vary shader intensity** (more bloom during peaks, more grain during quiet)
    93→- **Different particle types** if particles are active
    94→
    95→### Project-Specific Invention
    96→
    97→For every project, invent at least one of:
    98→- A custom character palette matching the theme
    99→- A custom background effect (combine/modify existing building blocks)
   100→- A custom color palette (discrete RGB set matching the brand/mood)
   101→- A custom particle character set
   102→- A novel scene transition or visual moment
   103→
   104→Don't just pick from the catalog. The catalog is vocabulary — you write the poem.
   105→
   106→## Workflow
   107→
   108→### Step 1: Creative Vision
   109→
   110→Before any code, articulate the creative concept:
   111→
   112→- **Mood/atmosphere**: What should the viewer feel? Energetic, meditative, chaotic, elegant, ominous?
   113→- **Visual story**: What happens over the duration? Build tension? Transform? Dissolve?
   114→- **Color world**: Warm/cool? Monochrome? Neon? Earth tones? What's the dominant hue?
   115→- **Character texture**: Dense data? Sparse stars? Organic dots? Geometric blocks?
   116→- **What makes THIS different**: What's the one thing that makes this project unique?
   117→- **Emotional arc**: How do scenes progress? Open with energy, build to climax, resolve?
   118→
   119→Map the user's prompt to aesthetic choices. A "chill lo-fi visualizer" demands different everything from a "glitch cyberpunk data stream."
   120→
   121→### Step 2: Technical Design
   122→
   123→- **Mode** — which of the 6 modes above
   124→- **Resolution** — landscape 1920x1080 (default), portrait 1080x1920, square 1080x1080 @ 24fps
   125→- **Hardware detection** — auto-detect cores/RAM, set quality profile. See `references/optimization.md`
   126→- **Sections** — map timestamps to scene functions, each with its own effect/palette/color/shader config
   127→- **Output format** — MP4 (default), GIF (640x360 @ 15fps), PNG sequence
   128→
   129→### Step 3: Build the Script
   130→
   131→Single Python file. Components (with references):
   132→
   133→1. **Hardware detection + quality profile** — `references/optimization.md`
   134→2. **Input loader** — mode-dependent; `references/inputs.md`
   135→3. **Feature analyzer** — audio FFT, video luminance, or synthetic
   136→4. **Grid + renderer** — multi-density grids with bitmap cache; `references/architecture.md`
   137→5. **Character palettes** — multiple per project; `references/architecture.md` § Palettes
   138→6. **Color system** — HSV + discrete RGB + harmony generation; `references/architecture.md` § Color
   139→7. **Scene functions** — each returns `canvas (uint8 H,W,3)`; `references/scenes.md`
   140→8. **Tonemap** — adaptive brightness normalization; `references/composition.md`
   141→9. **Shader pipeline** — `ShaderChain` + `FeedbackBuffer`; `references/shaders.md`
   142→10. **Scene table + dispatcher** — time → scene function + config; `references/scenes.md`
   143→11. **Parallel encoder** — N-worker clip rendering with ffmpeg pipes
   144→12. **Main** — orchestrate full pipeline
   145→
   146→### Step 4: Quality Verification
   147→
   148→- **Test frames first**: render single frames at key timestamps before full render
   149→- **Brightness check**: `canvas.mean() > 8` for all ASCII content. If dark, lower gamma
   150→- **Visual coherence**: do all scenes feel like they belong to the same video?
   151→- **Creative vision check**: does the output match the concept from Step 1? If it looks generic, go back
   152→
   153→## Critical Implementation Notes
   154→
   155→### Brightness — Use `tonemap()`, Not Linear Multipliers
   156→
   157→This is the #1 visual issue. ASCII on black is inherently dark. **Never use `canvas * N` multipliers** — they clip highlights. Use adaptive tonemap:
   158→
   159→```python
   160→def tonemap(canvas, gamma=0.75):
   161→    f = canvas.astype(np.float32)
   162→    lo, hi = np.percentile(f[::4, ::4], [1, 99.5])
   163→    if hi - lo < 10: hi = lo + 10
   164→    f = np.clip((f - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1) ** gamma
   165→    return (f * 255).astype(np.uint8)
   166→```
   167→
   168→Pipeline: `scene_fn() → tonemap() → FeedbackBuffer → ShaderChain → ffmpeg`
   169→
   170→Per-scene gamma: default 0.75, solarize 0.55, posterize 0.50, bright scenes 0.85. Use `screen` blend (not `overlay`) for dark layers.
   171→
   172→### Font Cell Height
   173→
   174→macOS Pillow: `textbbox()` returns wrong height. Use `font.getmetrics()`: `cell_height = ascent + descent`. See `references/troubleshooting.md`.
   175→
   176→### ffmpeg Pipe Deadlock
   177→
   178→Never `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` with long-running ffmpeg — buffer fills at 64KB and deadlocks. Redirect to file. See `references/troubleshooting.md`.
   179→
   180→### Font Compatibility
   181→
   182→Not all Unicode chars render in all fonts. Validate palettes at init — render each char, check for blank output. See `references/troubleshooting.md`.
   183→
   184→### Per-Clip Architecture
   185→
   186→For segmented videos (quotes, scenes, chapters), render each as a separate clip file for parallel rendering and selective re-rendering. See `references/scenes.md`.
   187→
   188→## Performance Targets
   189→
   190→| Component | Budget |
   191→|-----------|--------|
   192→| Feature extraction | 1-5ms |
   193→| Effect function | 2-15ms |
   194→| Character render | 80-150ms (bottleneck) |
   195→| Shader pipeline | 5-25ms |
   196→| **Total** | ~100-200ms/frame |
   197→
   198→## References
   199→
   200→| File | Contents |
   201→|------|----------|
   202→| `references/architecture.md` | Grid system, resolution presets, font selection, character palettes (20+), color system (HSV + OKLAB + discrete RGB + harmony generation), `_render_vf()` helper, GridLayer class |
   203→| `references/composition.md` | Pixel blend modes (20 modes), `blend_canvas()`, multi-grid composition, adaptive `tonemap()`, `FeedbackBuffer`, `PixelBlendStack`, masking/stencil system |
   204→| `references/effects.md` | Effect building blocks: value field generators, hue fields, noise/fBM/domain warp, voronoi, reaction-diffusion, cellular automata, SDFs, strange attractors, particle systems, coordinate transforms, temporal coherence |
   205→| `references/shaders.md` | `ShaderChain`, `_apply_shader_step()` dispatch, 38 shader catalog, audio-reactive scaling, transitions, tint presets, output format encoding, terminal rendering |
   206→| `references/scenes.md` | Scene protocol, `Renderer` class, `SCENES` table, `render_clip()`, beat-synced cutting, parallel rendering, design patterns (layer hierarchy, directional arcs, visual metaphors, compositional techniques), complete scene examples at every complexity level, scene design checklist |
   207→| `references/inputs.md` | Audio analysis (FFT, bands, beats), video sampling, image conversion, text/lyrics, TTS integration (ElevenLabs, voice assignment, audio mixing) |
   208→| `references/optimization.md` | Hardware detection, quality profiles, vectorized patterns, parallel rendering, memory management, performance budgets |
   209→| `references/troubleshooting.md` | NumPy broadcasting traps, blend mode pitfalls, multiprocessing/pickling, brightness diagnostics, ffmpeg issues, font problems, common mistakes |
   210→

   212→
   213→## Creative Divergence (use only when user requests experimental/creative/unique output)
   214→
   215→If the user asks for creative, experimental, surprising, or unconventional output, select the strategy that best fits and reason through its steps BEFORE generating code.
   216→
   217→- **Forced Connections** — when the user wants cross-domain inspiration ("make it look organic," "industrial aesthetic")
   218→- **Conceptual Blending** — when the user names two things to combine ("ocean meets music," "space + calligraphy")
   219→- **Oblique Strategies** — when the user is maximally open ("surprise me," "something I've never seen")
   220→
   221→### Forced Connections
   222→1. Pick a domain unrelated to the visual goal (weather systems, microbiology, architecture, fluid dynamics, textile weaving)
   223→2. List its core visual/structural elements (erosion → gradual reveal; mitosis → splitting duplication; weaving → interlocking patterns)
   224→3. Map those elements onto ASCII characters and animation patterns
   225→4. Synthesize — what does "erosion" or "crystallization" look like in a character grid?
   226→
   227→### Conceptual Blending
   228→1. Name two distinct visual/conceptual spaces (e.g., ocean waves + sheet music)
   229→2. Map correspondences (crests = high notes, troughs = rests, foam = staccato)
   230→3. Blend selectively — keep the most interesting mappings, discard forced ones
   231→4. Develop emergent properties that exist only in the blend
   232→
   233→### Oblique Strategies
   234→1. Draw one: "Honor thy error as a hidden intention" / "Use an old idea" / "What would your closest friend do?" / "Emphasize the flaws" / "Turn it upside down" / "Only a part, not the whole" / "Reverse"
   235→2. Interpret the directive against the current ASCII animation challenge
   236→3. Apply the lateral insight to the visual design before writing code
   237→

   146→## Workflow
   147→
   148→### Step 1: Analyze Content
   149→
   150→**Load references**: Read `references/analysis-framework.md` from this skill.
   151→
   152→1. Save source content (file path or paste → `source.md` using `write_file`)
   153→   - **Backup rule**: If `source.md` exists, rename to `source-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.md`
   154→2. Analyze: topic, data type, complexity, tone, audience
   155→3. Detect source language and user language
   156→4. Extract design instructions from user input
   157→5. Save analysis to `analysis.md`
   158→   - **Backup rule**: If `analysis.md` exists, rename to `analysis-backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.md`
   159→
   160→See `references/analysis-framework.md` for detailed format.
   161→
   162→### Step 2: Generate Structured Content → `structured-content.md`
   163→
   164→Transform content into infographic structure:
   165→1. Title and learning objectives
   166→2. Sections with: key concept, content (verbatim), visual element, text labels
   167→3. Data points (all statistics/quotes copied exactly)
   168→4. Design instructions from user
   169→
   170→**Rules**: Markdown only. No new information. Preserve data faithfully. Strip any credentials or secrets from output.
   171→
   172→See `references/structured-content-template.md` for detailed format.
