     2→name: github-code-review
     3→description: Review code changes by analyzing git diffs, leaving inline comments on PRs, and performing thorough pre-push review. Works with gh CLI or falls back to git + GitHub REST API via curl.
     4→version: 1.1.0
     5→author: Hermes Agent
     6→license: MIT
     7→metadata:
     8→  hermes:
     9→    tags: [GitHub, Code-Review, Pull-Requests, Git, Quality]
    10→    related_skills: [github-auth, github-pr-workflow]
    11→origin:
    12→  source: hermes-agent
    13→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    14→  version: 9f22977f
    15→---
    16→
    17→# GitHub Code Review
    18→
    19→Perform code reviews on local changes before pushing, or review open PRs on GitHub. Most of this skill uses plain `git` — the `gh`/`curl` split only matters for PR-level interactions.
    20→
    21→## Prerequisites
    22→
    23→- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)
    24→- Inside a git repository
    25→
    26→### Setup (for PR interactions)
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
    30→  AUTH="gh"
    31→else
    32→  AUTH="git"
    33→  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    34→    if [ -f ~/.hermes/.env ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env; then
    35→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    36→    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
    37→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|https://[^:]*:\([^@]*\)@.*|\1|')
    38→    fi
    39→  fi
    40→fi
    41→
    42→REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
    43→OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
    44→OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
    45→REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
    46→```
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## 1. Reviewing Local Changes (Pre-Push)
    51→
    52→This is pure `git` — works everywhere, no API needed.
    53→
    54→### Get the Diff
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→# Staged changes (what would be committed)
    58→git diff --staged
    59→
    60→# All changes vs main (what a PR would contain)
    61→git diff main...HEAD
    62→
    63→# File names only
    64→git diff main...HEAD --name-only
    65→
    66→# Stat summary (insertions/deletions per file)
    67→git diff main...HEAD --stat
    68→```
    69→
    70→### Review Strategy
    71→
    72→1. **Get the big picture first:**
    73→
    74→```bash
    75→git diff main...HEAD --stat
    76→git log main..HEAD --oneline
    77→```
    78→
    79→2. **Review file by file** — use `read_file` on changed files for full context, and the diff to see what changed:
    80→
    81→```bash
    82→git diff main...HEAD -- src/auth/login.py
    83→```
    84→
    85→3. **Check for common issues:**
    86→
    87→```bash
    88→# Debug statements, TODOs, console.logs left behind
    89→git diff main...HEAD | grep -n "print(\|console\.log\|TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX\|debugger"
    90→
    91→# Large files accidentally staged
    92→git diff main...HEAD --stat | sort -t'|' -k2 -rn | head -10
    93→
    94→# Secrets or credential patterns
    95→git diff main...HEAD | grep -in "password\|secret\|api_key\|token.*=\|private_key"
    96→
    97→# Merge conflict markers
    98→git diff main...HEAD | grep -n "<<<<<<\|>>>>>>\|======="
    99→```
   100→
   101→4. **Present structured feedback** to the user.
   102→
   103→### Review Output Format
   104→
   105→When reviewing local changes, present findings in this structure:
   106→
   107→```
   108→## Code Review Summary
   109→
   110→### Critical
   111→- **src/auth.py:45** — SQL injection: user input passed directly to query.
   112→  Suggestion: Use parameterized queries.
   113→
   114→### Warnings
   115→- **src/models/user.py:23** — Password stored in plaintext. Use bcrypt or argon2.
   116→- **src/api/routes.py:112** — No rate limiting on login endpoint.
   117→
   118→### Suggestions
   119→- **src/utils/helpers.py:8** — Duplicates logic in `src/core/utils.py:34`. Consolidate.
   120→- **tests/test_auth.py** — Missing edge case: expired token test.
   121→
   122→### Looks Good
   123→- Clean separation of concerns in the middleware layer
   124→- Good test coverage for the happy path
   125→```
   126→
   127→---
   128→
   129→## 2. Reviewing a Pull Request on GitHub
   130→
   131→### View PR Details
   132→
   133→**With gh:**
   134→
   135→```bash
   136→gh pr view 123
   137→gh pr diff 123
   138→gh pr diff 123 --name-only
   139→```
   140→
   141→**With git + curl:**
   142→
   143→```bash
   144→PR_NUMBER=123
   145→
   146→# Get PR details
   147→curl -s \
   148→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   149→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
   150→  | python3 -c "
   151→import sys, json
   152→pr = json.load(sys.stdin)
   153→print(f\"Title: {pr['title']}\")
   154→print(f\"Author: {pr['user']['login']}\")
   155→print(f\"Branch: {pr['head']['ref']} -> {pr['base']['ref']}\")
   156→print(f\"State: {pr['state']}\")
   157→print(f\"Body:\n{pr['body']}\")"
   158→
   159→# List changed files
   160→curl -s \
   161→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   162→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files \
   163→  | python3 -c "
   164→import sys, json
   165→for f in json.load(sys.stdin):
   166→    print(f\"{f['status']:10} +{f['additions']:-4} -{f['deletions']:-4}  {f['filename']}\")"
   167→```
   168→
   169→### Check Out PR Locally for Full Review
   170→
   171→This works with plain `git` — no `gh` needed:
   172→
   173→```bash
   174→# Fetch the PR branch and check it out
   175→git fetch origin pull/123/head:pr-123
   176→git checkout pr-123
   177→
   178→# Now you can use read_file, search_files, run tests, etc.
   179→
   180→# View diff against the base branch
   181→git diff main...pr-123
   182→```
   183→
   184→**With gh (shortcut):**
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→gh pr checkout 123
   188→```
   189→
   190→### Leave Comments on a PR
   191→
   192→**General PR comment — with gh:**
   193→
   194→```bash
   195→gh pr comment 123 --body "Overall looks good, a few suggestions below."
   196→```
   197→
   198→**General PR comment — with curl:**
   199→
   200→```bash
   201→curl -s -X POST \
   202→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   203→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
   204→  -d '{"body": "Overall looks good, a few suggestions below."}'
   205→```
   206→
   207→### Leave Inline Review Comments
   208→
   209→**Single inline comment — with gh (via API):**
   210→
   211→```bash
   212→HEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view 123 --json headRefOid --jq '.headRefOid')
   213→
   214→gh api repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/123/comments \
   215→  --method POST \
   216→  -f body="This could be simplified with a list comprehension." \
   217→  -f path="src/auth/login.py" \
   218→  -f commit_id="$HEAD_SHA" \
   219→  -f line=45 \
   220→  -f side="RIGHT"
   221→```
   222→
   223→**Single inline comment — with curl:**
   224→
   225→```bash
   226→# Get the head commit SHA
   227→HEAD_SHA=$(curl -s \
   228→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   229→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
   230→  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])")
   231→
   232→curl -s -X POST \
   233→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   234→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
   235→  -d "{
   236→    \"body\": \"This could be simplified with a list comprehension.\",
   237→    \"path\": \"src/auth/login.py\",
   238→    \"commit_id\": \"$HEAD_SHA\",
   239→    \"line\": 45,
   240→    \"side\": \"RIGHT\"
   241→  }"
   242→```
   243→
   244→### Submit a Formal Review (Approve / Request Changes)
   245→
   246→**With gh:**
   247→
   248→```bash
   249→gh pr review 123 --approve --body "LGTM!"
   250→gh pr review 123 --request-changes --body "See inline comments."
   251→gh pr review 123 --comment --body "Some suggestions, nothing blocking."
   252→```
   253→
   254→**With curl — multi-comment review submitted atomically:**
   255→
   256→```bash
   257→HEAD_SHA=$(curl -s \
   258→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   259→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
   260→  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])")
   261→
   262→curl -s -X POST \
   263→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   264→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/reviews \
   265→  -d "{
   266→    \"commit_id\": \"$HEAD_SHA\",
   267→    \"event\": \"COMMENT\",
   268→    \"body\": \"Code review from Hermes Agent\",
   269→    \"comments\": [
   270→      {\"path\": \"src/auth.py\", \"line\": 45, \"body\": \"Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection.\"},
   271→      {\"path\": \"src/models/user.py\", \"line\": 23, \"body\": \"Hash passwords with bcrypt before storing.\"},
   272→      {\"path\": \"tests/test_auth.py\", \"line\": 1, \"body\": \"Add test for expired token edge case.\"}
   273→    ]
   274→  }"
   275→```
   276→
   277→Event values: `"APPROVE"`, `"REQUEST_CHANGES"`, `"COMMENT"`
   278→
   279→The `line` field refers to the line number in the *new* version of the file. For deleted lines, use `"side": "LEFT"`.
   280→
   281→---
   282→
   283→## 3. Review Checklist
   284→
   285→When performing a code review (local or PR), systematically check:
   286→
   287→### Correctness
   288→- Does the code do what it claims?
   289→- Edge cases handled (empty inputs, nulls, large data, concurrent access)?
   290→- Error paths handled gracefully?
   291→
   292→### Security
   293→- No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or API keys
   294→- Input validation on user-facing inputs
   295→- No SQL injection, XSS, or path traversal
   296→- Auth/authz checks where needed
   297→
   298→### Code Quality
   299→- Clear naming (variables, functions, classes)
   300→- No unnecessary complexity or premature abstraction
   301→- DRY — no duplicated logic that should be extracted
   302→- Functions are focused (single responsibility)
   303→
   304→### Testing
   305→- New code paths tested?
   306→- Happy path and error cases covered?
   307→- Tests readable and maintainable?
   308→
   309→### Performance
   310→- No N+1 queries or unnecessary loops
   311→- Appropriate caching where beneficial
   312→- No blocking operations in async code paths
   313→
   314→### Documentation
   315→- Public APIs documented
   316→- Non-obvious logic has comments explaining "why"
   317→- README updated if behavior changed
   318→
   319→---
   320→
   321→## 4. Pre-Push Review Workflow
   322→
   323→When the user asks you to "review the code" or "check before pushing":
   324→
   325→1. `git diff main...HEAD --stat` — see scope of changes
   326→2. `git diff main...HEAD` — read the full diff
   327→3. For each changed file, use `read_file` if you need more context
   328→4. Apply the checklist above
   329→5. Present findings in the structured format (Critical / Warnings / Suggestions / Looks Good)
   330→6. If critical issues found, offer to fix them before the user pushes
   331→
   332→---
   333→
   334→## 5. PR Review Workflow (End-to-End)
   335→
   336→When the user asks you to "review PR #N", "look at this PR", or gives you a PR URL, follow this recipe:
   337→
   338→### Step 1: Set up environment
   339→
   340→```bash
   341→source "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/gh-env.sh"
   342→# Or run the inline setup block from the top of this skill
   343→```
   344→
   345→### Step 2: Gather PR context
   346→
   347→Get the PR metadata, description, and list of changed files to understand scope before diving into code.
   348→
   349→**With gh:**
   350→```bash
   351→gh pr view 123
   352→gh pr diff 123 --name-only
   353→gh pr checks 123
   354→```
   355→
   356→**With curl:**
   357→```bash
   358→PR_NUMBER=123
   359→
   360→# PR details (title, author, description, branch)
   361→curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   362→  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER
   363→
   364→# Changed files with line counts
   365→curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   366→  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/files
   367→```
   368→
   369→### Step 3: Check out the PR locally
   370→
   371→This gives you full access to `read_file`, `search_files`, and the ability to run tests.
   372→
   373→```bash
   374→git fetch origin pull/$PR_NUMBER/head:pr-$PR_NUMBER
   375→git checkout pr-$PR_NUMBER
   376→```
   377→
   378→### Step 4: Read the diff and understand changes
   379→
   380→```bash
   381→# Full diff against the base branch
   382→git diff main...HEAD
   383→
   384→# Or file-by-file for large PRs
   385→git diff main...HEAD --name-only
   386→# Then for each file:
   387→git diff main...HEAD -- path/to/file.py
   388→```
   389→
   390→For each changed file, use `read_file` to see full context around the changes — diffs alone can miss issues visible only with surrounding code.
   391→
   392→### Step 5: Run automated checks locally (if applicable)
   393→
   394→```bash
   395→# Run tests if there's a test suite
   396→python -m pytest 2>&1 | tail -20
   397→# or: npm test, cargo test, go test ./..., etc.
   398→
   399→# Run linter if configured
   400→ruff check . 2>&1 | head -30
   401→# or: eslint, clippy, etc.
   402→```
   403→
   404→### Step 6: Apply the review checklist (Section 3)
   405→
   406→Go through each category: Correctness, Security, Code Quality, Testing, Performance, Documentation.
   407→
   408→### Step 7: Post the review to GitHub
   409→
   410→Collect your findings and submit them as a formal review with inline comments.
   411→
   412→**With gh:**
   413→```bash
   414→# If no issues — approve
   415→gh pr review $PR_NUMBER --approve --body "Reviewed by Hermes Agent. Code looks clean — good test coverage, no security concerns."
   416→
   417→# If issues found — request changes with inline comments
   418→gh pr review $PR_NUMBER --request-changes --body "Found a few issues — see inline comments."
   419→```
   420→
   421→**With curl — atomic review with multiple inline comments:**
   422→```bash
   423→HEAD_SHA=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   424→  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
   425→  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['head']['sha'])")
   426→
   427→# Build the review JSON — event is APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, or COMMENT
   428→curl -s -X POST \
   429→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   430→  https://api.github.com/repos/$GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/reviews \
   431→  -d "{
   432→    \"commit_id\": \"$HEAD_SHA\",
   433→    \"event\": \"REQUEST_CHANGES\",
   434→    \"body\": \"## Hermes Agent Review\n\nFound 2 issues, 1 suggestion. See inline comments.\",
   435→    \"comments\": [
   436→      {\"path\": \"src/auth.py\", \"line\": 45, \"body\": \"🔴 **Critical:** User input passed directly to SQL query — use parameterized queries.\"},
   437→      {\"path\": \"src/models.py\", \"line\": 23, \"body\": \"⚠️ **Warning:** Password stored without hashing.\"},
   438→      {\"path\": \"src/utils.py\", \"line\": 8, \"body\": \"💡 **Suggestion:** This duplicates logic in core/utils.py:34.\"}
   439→    ]
   440→  }"
   441→```
   442→
   443→### Step 8: Also post a summary comment
   444→
   445→In addition to inline comments, leave a top-level summary so the PR author gets the full picture at a glance. Use the review output format from `references/review-output-template.md`.
   446→
   447→**With gh:**
   448→```bash
   449→gh pr comment $PR_NUMBER --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
   450→## Code Review Summary
   451→
   452→**Verdict: Changes Requested** (2 issues, 1 suggestion)
   453→
   454→### 🔴 Critical
   455→- **src/auth.py:45** — SQL injection vulnerability
   456→
   457→### ⚠️ Warnings
   458→- **src/models.py:23** — Plaintext password storage
   459→
   460→### 💡 Suggestions
   461→- **src/utils.py:8** — Duplicated logic, consider consolidating
   462→
   463→### ✅ Looks Good
   464→- Clean API design
   465→- Good error handling in the middleware layer
   466→
   467→---
   468→*Reviewed by Hermes Agent*
   469→EOF
   470→)"
   471→```
   472→
   473→### Step 9: Clean up
   474→
   475→```bash
   476→git checkout main
   477→git branch -D pr-$PR_NUMBER
   478→```
   479→
   480→### Decision: Approve vs Request Changes vs Comment
   481→
   482→- **Approve** — no critical or warning-level issues, only minor suggestions or all clear
   483→- **Request Changes** — any critical or warning-level issue that should be fixed before merge
   484→- **Comment** — observations and suggestions, but nothing blocking (use when you're unsure or the PR is a draft)
   485→

    17→# GitHub Issues Management
    18→
    19→Create, search, triage, and manage GitHub issues. Each section shows `gh` first, then the `curl` fallback.
    20→
    21→## Prerequisites
    22→
    23→- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)
    24→- Inside a git repo with a GitHub remote, or specify the repo explicitly
    25→
    26→### Setup
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
    30→  AUTH="gh"
    31→else
    32→  AUTH="git"
    33→  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    34→    if [ -f ~/.hermes/.env ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env; then
    35→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    36→    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
    37→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|https://[^:]*:\([^@]*\)@.*|\1|')
    38→    fi
    39→  fi
    40→fi
    41→
    42→REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
    43→OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
    44→OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
    45→REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
    46→```
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## 1. Viewing Issues
    51→
    52→**With gh:**
    53→
    54→```bash
    55→gh issue list
    56→gh issue list --state open --label "bug"
    57→gh issue list --assignee @me
    58→gh issue list --search "authentication error" --state all
    59→gh issue view 42
    60→```
    61→
    62→**With curl:**
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→# List open issues
    66→curl -s \
    67→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    68→  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?state=open&per_page=20" \
    69→  | python3 -c "
    70→import sys, json
    71→for i in json.load(sys.stdin):
    72→    if 'pull_request' not in i:  # GitHub API returns PRs in /issues too
    73→        labels = ', '.join(l['name'] for l in i['labels'])
    74→        print(f\"#{i['number']:5}  {i['state']:6}  {labels:30}  {i['title']}\")"
    75→
    76→# Filter by label
    77→curl -s \
    78→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    79→  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?state=open&labels=bug&per_page=20" \
    80→  | python3 -c "
    81→import sys, json
    82→for i in json.load(sys.stdin):
    83→    if 'pull_request' not in i:
    84→        print(f\"#{i['number']}  {i['title']}\")"
    85→
    86→# View a specific issue
    87→curl -s \
    88→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    89→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \
    90→  | python3 -c "
    91→import sys, json
    92→i = json.load(sys.stdin)
    93→labels = ', '.join(l['name'] for l in i['labels'])
    94→assignees = ', '.join(a['login'] for a in i['assignees'])
    95→print(f\"#{i['number']}: {i['title']}\")
    96→print(f\"State: {i['state']}  Labels: {labels}  Assignees: {assignees}\")
    97→print(f\"Author: {i['user']['login']}  Created: {i['created_at']}\")
    98→print(f\"\n{i['body']}\")"
    99→
   100→# Search issues
   101→curl -s \
   102→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   103→  "https://api.github.com/search/issues?q=authentication+error+repo:$OWNER/$REPO" \
   104→  | python3 -c "
   105→import sys, json
   106→for i in json.load(sys.stdin)['items']:
   107→    print(f\"#{i['number']}  {i['state']:6}  {i['title']}\")"
   108→```
   109→
   110→## 2. Creating Issues
   111→
   112→**With gh:**
   113→
   114→```bash
   115→gh issue create \
   116→  --title "Login redirect ignores ?next= parameter" \
   117→  --body "## Description
   118→After logging in, users always land on /dashboard.
   119→
   120→## Steps to Reproduce
   121→1. Navigate to /settings while logged out
   122→2. Get redirected to /login?next=/settings
   123→3. Log in
   124→4. Actual: redirected to /dashboard (should go to /settings)
   125→
   126→## Expected Behavior
   127→Respect the ?next= query parameter." \
   128→  --label "bug,backend" \
   129→  --assignee "username"
   130→```
   131→
   132→**With curl:**
   133→
   134→```bash
   135→curl -s -X POST \
   136→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   137→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues \
   138→  -d '{
   139→    "title": "Login redirect ignores ?next= parameter",
   140→    "body": "## Description\nAfter logging in, users always land on /dashboard.\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n1. Navigate to /settings while logged out\n2. Get redirected to /login?next=/settings\n3. Log in\n4. Actual: redirected to /dashboard\n\n## Expected Behavior\nRespect the ?next= query parameter.",
   141→    "labels": ["bug", "backend"],
   142→    "assignees": ["username"]
   143→  }'
   144→```

   146→### Bug Report Template
   147→

   182→
   183→## 3. Managing Issues
   184→
   185→### Add/Remove Labels
   186→
   187→**With gh:**
   188→
   189→```bash
   190→gh issue edit 42 --add-label "priority:high,bug"
   191→gh issue edit 42 --remove-label "needs-triage"
   192→```
   193→
   194→**With curl:**
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→# Add labels
   198→curl -s -X POST \
   199→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   200→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/labels \
   201→  -d '{"labels": ["priority:high", "bug"]}'
   202→
   203→# Remove a label
   204→curl -s -X DELETE \
   205→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   206→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/labels/needs-triage
   207→
   208→# List available labels in the repo
   209→curl -s \
   210→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   211→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/labels \
   212→  | python3 -c "
   213→import sys, json
   214→for l in json.load(sys.stdin):
   215→    print(f\"  {l['name']:30}  {l.get('description', '')}\")"
   216→```
   217→
   218→### Assignment
   219→
   220→**With gh:**
   221→
   222→```bash
   223→gh issue edit 42 --add-assignee username
   224→gh issue edit 42 --add-assignee @me
   225→```
   226→
   227→**With curl:**
   228→
   229→```bash
   230→curl -s -X POST \
   231→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   232→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/assignees \
   233→  -d '{"assignees": ["username"]}'
   234→```
   235→
   236→### Commenting
   237→
   238→**With gh:**
   239→
   240→```bash
   241→gh issue comment 42 --body "Investigated — root cause is in auth middleware. Working on a fix."
   242→```
   243→
   244→**With curl:**
   245→
   246→```bash
   247→curl -s -X POST \
   248→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   249→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42/comments \
   250→  -d '{"body": "Investigated — root cause is in auth middleware. Working on a fix."}'
   251→```
   252→
   253→### Closing and Reopening
   254→
   255→**With gh:**
   256→
   257→```bash
   258→gh issue close 42
   259→gh issue close 42 --reason "not planned"
   260→gh issue reopen 42
   261→```
   262→
   263→**With curl:**
   264→
   265→```bash
   266→# Close
   267→curl -s -X PATCH \
   268→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   269→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \
   270→  -d '{"state": "closed", "state_reason": "completed"}'
   271→
   272→# Reopen
   273→curl -s -X PATCH \
   274→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   275→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/42 \
   276→  -d '{"state": "open"}'
   277→```
   278→
   279→### Linking Issues to PRs
   280→
   281→Issues are automatically closed when a PR merges with the right keywords in the body:
   282→
   283→```
   284→Closes #42
   285→Fixes #42
   286→Resolves #42
   287→```
   288→
   289→To create a branch from an issue:
   290→
   291→**With gh:**
   292→
   293→```bash
   294→gh issue develop 42 --checkout
   295→```
   296→
   297→**With git (manual equivalent):**
   298→
   299→```bash
   300→git checkout main && git pull origin main
   301→git checkout -b fix/issue-42-login-redirect
   302→```
   303→
   304→## 4. Issue Triage Workflow
   305→
   306→When asked to triage issues:
   307→
   308→1. **List untriaged issues:**
   309→
   310→```bash
   311→# With gh
   312→gh issue list --label "needs-triage" --state open
   313→
   314→# With curl
   315→curl -s \
   316→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   317→  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?labels=needs-triage&state=open" \
   318→  | python3 -c "
   319→import sys, json
   320→for i in json.load(sys.stdin):
   321→    if 'pull_request' not in i:
   322→        print(f\"#{i['number']}  {i['title']}\")"
   323→```
   324→
   325→2. **Read and categorize** each issue (view details, understand the bug/feature)
   326→
   327→3. **Apply labels and priority** (see Managing Issues above)
   328→
   329→4. **Assign** if the owner is clear
   330→
   331→5. **Comment with triage notes** if needed
   332→
   333→## 5. Bulk Operations
   334→
   335→For batch operations, combine API calls with shell scripting:
   336→
   337→**With gh:**
   338→
   339→```bash
   340→# Close all issues with a specific label
   341→gh issue list --label "wontfix" --json number --jq '.[].number' | \
   342→  xargs -I {} gh issue close {} --reason "not planned"
   343→```
   344→
   345→**With curl:**
   346→
   347→```bash
   348→# List issue numbers with a label, then close each
   349→curl -s \
   350→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   351→  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues?labels=wontfix&state=open" \
   352→  | python3 -c "import sys,json; [print(i['number']) for i in json.load(sys.stdin)]" \
   353→  | while read num; do
   354→    curl -s -X PATCH \
   355→      -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   356→      https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/$num \
   357→      -d '{"state": "closed", "state_reason": "not_planned"}'
   358→    echo "Closed #$num"
   359→  done
   360→```
   361→
   362→## Quick Reference Table
   363→
   364→| Action | gh | curl endpoint |
   365→|--------|-----|--------------|
   366→| List issues | `gh issue list` | `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` |
   367→| View issue | `gh issue view N` | `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N` |
   368→| Create issue | `gh issue create ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` |
   369→| Add labels | `gh issue edit N --add-label ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/labels` |
   370→| Assign | `gh issue edit N --add-assignee ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/assignees` |
   371→| Comment | `gh issue comment N --body ...` | `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N/comments` |
   372→| Close | `gh issue close N` | `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/N` |
   373→| Search | `gh issue list --search "..."` | `GET /search/issues?q=...` |
   374→

    39→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|https://[^:]*:\([^@]*\)@.*|\1|')
    40→    fi
    41→  fi
    42→fi
    43→echo "Using: $AUTH"
    44→```
    45→
    46→### Extracting Owner/Repo from the Git Remote
    47→
    48→Many `curl` commands need `owner/repo`. Extract it from the git remote:
    49→
    50→```bash
    51→# Works for both HTTPS and SSH remote URLs
    52→REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
    53→OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
    54→OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
    55→REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
    56→echo "Owner: $OWNER, Repo: $REPO"
    57→```

    60→
    61→## 1. Branch Creation
    62→
    63→This part is pure `git` — identical either way:
    64→
    65→```bash
    66→# Make sure you're up to date
    67→git fetch origin
    68→git checkout main && git pull origin main
    69→
    70→# Create and switch to a new branch
    71→git checkout -b feat/add-user-authentication
    72→```
    73→
    74→Branch naming conventions:
    75→- `feat/description` — new features
    76→- `fix/description` — bug fixes
    77→- `refactor/description` — code restructuring
    78→- `docs/description` — documentation
    79→- `ci/description` — CI/CD changes
    80→
    81→## 2. Making Commits
    82→
    83→Use the agent's file tools (`write_file`, `patch`) to make changes, then commit:
    84→
    85→```bash
    86→# Stage specific files
    87→git add src/auth.py src/models/user.py tests/test_auth.py
    88→
    89→# Commit with a conventional commit message
    90→git commit -m "feat: add JWT-based user authentication
    91→
    92→- Add login/register endpoints
    93→- Add User model with password hashing
    94→- Add auth middleware for protected routes
    95→- Add unit tests for auth flow"
    96→```
    97→
    98→Commit message format (Conventional Commits):
    99→```
   100→type(scope): short description
   101→
   102→Longer explanation if needed. Wrap at 72 characters.
   103→```
   104→
   105→Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`
   106→
   107→## 3. Pushing and Creating a PR
   108→
   109→### Push the Branch (same either way)
   110→
   111→```bash
   112→git push -u origin HEAD
   113→```
   114→
   115→### Create the PR
   116→
   117→**With gh:**
   118→
   119→```bash
   120→gh pr create \
   121→  --title "feat: add JWT-based user authentication" \
   122→  --body "## Summary
   123→- Adds login and register API endpoints
   124→- JWT token generation and validation
   125→
   126→## Test Plan
   127→- [ ] Unit tests pass
   128→
   129→Closes #42"
   130→```
   131→
   132→Options: `--draft`, `--reviewer user1,user2`, `--label "enhancement"`, `--base develop`
   133→
   134→**With git + curl:**
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
   138→
   139→curl -s -X POST \
   140→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   141→  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" \
   142→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls \
   143→  -d "{
   144→    \"title\": \"feat: add JWT-based user authentication\",
   145→    \"body\": \"## Summary\nAdds login and register API endpoints.\n\nCloses #42\",
   146→    \"head\": \"$BRANCH\",
   147→    \"base\": \"main\"
   148→  }"
   149→```
   150→
   151→The response JSON includes the PR `number` — save it for later commands.
   152→
   153→To create as a draft, add `"draft": true` to the JSON body.
   154→
   155→## 4. Monitoring CI Status
   156→
   157→### Check CI Status
   158→
   159→**With gh:**
   160→
   161→```bash
   162→# One-shot check
   163→gh pr checks
   164→
   165→# Watch until all checks finish (polls every 10s)
   166→gh pr checks --watch
   167→```
   168→
   169→**With git + curl:**
   170→
   171→```bash
   172→# Get the latest commit SHA on the current branch
   173→SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
   174→
   175→# Query the combined status
   176→curl -s \
   177→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   178→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
   179→  | python3 -c "
   180→import sys, json
   181→data = json.load(sys.stdin)
   182→print(f\"Overall: {data['state']}\")
   183→for s in data.get('statuses', []):
   184→    print(f\"  {s['context']}: {s['state']} - {s.get('description', '')}\")"
   185→
   186→# Also check GitHub Actions check runs (separate endpoint)
   187→curl -s \
   188→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   189→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/check-runs \
   190→  | python3 -c "
   191→import sys, json
   192→data = json.load(sys.stdin)
   193→for cr in data.get('check_runs', []):
   194→    print(f\"  {cr['name']}: {cr['status']} / {cr['conclusion'] or 'pending'}\")"
   195→```
   196→
   197→### Poll Until Complete (git + curl)
   198→
   199→```bash
   200→# Simple polling loop — check every 30 seconds, up to 10 minutes
   201→SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
   202→for i in $(seq 1 20); do
   203→  STATUS=$(curl -s \
   204→    -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   205→    https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
   206→    | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['state'])")
   207→  echo "Check $i: $STATUS"
   208→  if [ "$STATUS" = "success" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "failure" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "error" ]; then
   209→    break
   210→  fi
   211→  sleep 30
   212→done
   213→```
   214→
   215→## 5. Auto-Fixing CI Failures
   216→
   217→When CI fails, diagnose and fix. This loop works with either auth method.
   218→
   219→### Step 1: Get Failure Details
   220→
   221→**With gh:**
   222→
   223→```bash
   224→# List recent workflow runs on this branch
   225→gh run list --branch $(git branch --show-current) --limit 5
   226→
   227→# View failed logs
   228→gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
   229→```
   230→
   231→**With git + curl:**
   232→
   233→```bash
   234→BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
   235→
   236→# List workflow runs on this branch
   237→curl -s \
   238→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   239→  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs?branch=$BRANCH&per_page=5" \
   240→  | python3 -c "
   241→import sys, json
   242→runs = json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']
   243→for r in runs:
   244→    print(f\"Run {r['id']}: {r['name']} - {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"
   245→
   246→# Get failed job logs (download as zip, extract, read)
   247→RUN_ID=<run_id>
   248→curl -s -L \
   249→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   250→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
   251→  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
   252→cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs && cat ci-logs/*.txt
   253→```
   254→
   255→### Step 2: Fix and Push
   256→
   257→After identifying the issue, use file tools (`patch`, `write_file`) to fix it:
   258→
   259→```bash
   260→git add <fixed_files>
   261→git commit -m "fix: resolve CI failure in <check_name>"
   262→git push
   263→```
   264→
   265→### Step 3: Verify
   266→
   267→Re-check CI status using the commands from Section 4 above.
   268→
   269→### Auto-Fix Loop Pattern
   270→
   271→When asked to auto-fix CI, follow this loop:
   272→
   273→1. Check CI status → identify failures
   274→2. Read failure logs → understand the error
   275→3. Use `read_file` + `patch`/`write_file` → fix the code
   276→4. `git add . && git commit -m "fix: ..." && git push`
   277→5. Wait for CI → re-check status
   278→6. Repeat if still failing (up to 3 attempts, then ask the user)
   279→
   280→## 6. Merging
   281→
   282→**With gh:**
   283→
   284→```bash
   285→# Squash merge + delete branch (cleanest for feature branches)
   286→gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch
   287→
   288→# Enable auto-merge (merges when all checks pass)
   289→gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch
   290→```
   291→
   292→**With git + curl:**
   293→
   294→```bash
   295→PR_NUMBER=<number>
   296→
   297→# Merge the PR via API (squash)
   298→curl -s -X PUT \
   299→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   300→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/merge \
   301→  -d "{
   302→    \"merge_method\": \"squash\",
   303→    \"commit_title\": \"feat: add user authentication (#$PR_NUMBER)\"
   304→  }"
   305→
   306→# Delete the remote branch after merge
   307→BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
   308→git push origin --delete $BRANCH
   309→
   310→# Switch back to main locally
   311→git checkout main && git pull origin main
   312→git branch -d $BRANCH
   313→```
   314→
   315→Merge methods: `"merge"` (merge commit), `"squash"`, `"rebase"`
   316→
   317→### Enable Auto-Merge (curl)
   318→
   319→```bash
   320→# Auto-merge requires the repo to have it enabled in settings.
   321→# This uses the GraphQL API since REST doesn't support auto-merge.
   322→PR_NODE_ID=$(curl -s \
   323→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   324→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
   325→  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['node_id'])")
   326→
   327→curl -s -X POST \
   328→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   329→  https://api.github.com/graphql \
   330→  -d "{\"query\": \"mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: \\\"$PR_NODE_ID\\\", mergeMethod: SQUASH}) { clientMutationId } }\"}"
   331→```
   332→
   333→## 7. Complete Workflow Example
   334→
   335→```bash
   336→# 1. Start from clean main
   337→git checkout main && git pull origin main
   338→
   339→# 2. Branch
   340→git checkout -b fix/login-redirect-bug
   341→
   342→# 3. (Agent makes code changes with file tools)
   343→
   344→# 4. Commit
   345→git add src/auth/login.py tests/test_login.py
   346→git commit -m "fix: correct redirect URL after login
   347→
   348→Preserves the ?next= parameter instead of always redirecting to /dashboard."
   349→
   350→# 5. Push
   351→git push -u origin HEAD
   352→
   353→# 6. Create PR (picks gh or curl based on what's available)
   354→# ... (see Section 3)
   355→
   356→# 7. Monitor CI (see Section 4)
   357→
   358→# 8. Merge when green (see Section 6)

   362→
   363→| Action | gh | git + curl |
   364→|--------|-----|-----------|
   365→| List my PRs | `gh pr list --author @me` | `curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls?state=open"` |
   366→| View PR diff | `gh pr diff` | `git diff main...HEAD` (local) or `curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.diff" ...` |

    25→### Setup
    26→
    27→```bash
    28→if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
    29→  AUTH="gh"
    30→else
    31→  AUTH="git"
    32→  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    33→    if [ -f ~/.hermes/.env ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" ~/.hermes/.env; then

    36→      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null | head -1 | sed 's|https://[^:]*:\([^@]*\)@.*|\1|')
    37→    fi
    38→  fi
    39→fi
    40→
    41→# Get your GitHub username (needed for several operations)
    42→if [ "$AUTH" = "gh" ]; then
    43→  GH_USER=$(gh api user --jq '.login')
    44→else
    45→  GH_USER=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/user | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['login'])")

    59→
    60→## 1. Cloning Repositories
    61→
    62→Cloning is pure `git` — works identically either way:
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→# Clone via HTTPS (works with credential helper or token-embedded URL)
    66→git clone https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git
    67→
    68→# Clone into a specific directory
    69→git clone https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git ./my-local-dir
    70→
    71→# Shallow clone (faster for large repos)
    72→git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git
    73→
    74→# Clone a specific branch
    75→git clone --branch develop https://github.com/owner/repo-name.git
    76→
    77→# Clone via SSH (if SSH is configured)
    78→git clone git@github.com:owner/repo-name.git
    79→```
    80→
    81→**With gh (shorthand):**
    82→
    83→```bash
    84→gh repo clone owner/repo-name
    85→gh repo clone owner/repo-name -- --depth 1
    86→```
    87→
    88→## 2. Creating Repositories
    89→
    90→**With gh:**
    91→
    92→```bash
    93→# Create a public repo and clone it
    94→gh repo create my-new-project --public --clone
    95→
    96→# Private, with description and license
    97→gh repo create my-new-project --private --description "A useful tool" --license MIT --clone
    98→
    99→# Under an organization
   100→gh repo create my-org/my-new-project --public --clone
   101→
   102→# From existing local directory
   103→cd /path/to/existing/project
   104→gh repo create my-project --source . --public --push
   105→```
   106→
   107→**With git + curl:**
   108→
   109→```bash
   110→# Create the remote repo via API
   111→curl -s -X POST \
   112→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   113→  https://api.github.com/user/repos \
   114→  -d '{
   115→    "name": "my-new-project",
   116→    "description": "A useful tool",
   117→    "private": false,
   118→    "auto_init": true,
   119→    "license_template": "mit"
   120→  }'
   121→
   122→# Clone it
   123→git clone https://github.com/$GH_USER/my-new-project.git
   124→cd my-new-project
   125→
   126→# -- OR -- push an existing local directory to the new repo
   127→cd /path/to/existing/project
   128→git init
   129→git add .
   130→git commit -m "Initial commit"
   131→git remote add origin https://github.com/$GH_USER/my-new-project.git
   132→git push -u origin main
   133→```
   134→
   135→To create under an organization:
   136→
   137→```bash
   138→curl -s -X POST \
   139→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   140→  https://api.github.com/orgs/my-org/repos \
   141→  -d '{"name": "my-new-project", "private": false}'
   142→```
   143→
   144→### From a Template
   145→
   146→**With gh:**
   147→
   148→```bash
   149→gh repo create my-new-app --template owner/template-repo --public --clone
   150→```
   151→

   161→## 3. Forking Repositories

   163→**With gh:**

   281→
   282→```bash

   290→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   291→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/branches/main/protection \
   292→  -d '{
   293→    "required_status_checks": {
   294→      "strict": true,
   295→      "contexts": ["ci/test", "ci/lint"]
   296→    },
   297→    "enforce_admins": false,

   300→    },
   301→    "restrictions": null
   302→  }'
   303→```
   304→
   305→## 7. Secrets Management (GitHub Actions)
   306→
   307→**With gh:**
   308→
   309→```bash
   310→gh secret set API_KEY --body "your-secret-value"
   311→gh secret set SSH_KEY < ~/.ssh/id_rsa
   312→gh secret list
   313→gh secret delete API_KEY
   314→```
   315→
   316→**With curl:**
   317→
   318→Secrets require encryption with the repo's public key — more involved via API:
   319→
   320→```bash
   321→# Get the repo's public key for encrypting secrets
   322→curl -s \
   323→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   324→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets/public-key
   325→
   326→# Encrypt and set (requires Python with PyNaCl)
   327→python3 -c "
   328→from base64 import b64encode
   329→from nacl import encoding, public
   330→import json, sys
   331→
   332→# Get the public key
   333→key_id = '<key_id_from_above>'
   334→public_key = '<base64_key_from_above>'
   335→
   336→# Encrypt
   337→sealed = public.SealedBox(
   338→    public.PublicKey(public_key.encode('utf-8'), encoding.Base64Encoder)
   339→).encrypt('your-secret-value'.encode('utf-8'))
   340→print(json.dumps({
   341→    'encrypted_value': b64encode(sealed).decode('utf-8'),
   342→    'key_id': key_id
   343→}))"
   344→
   345→# Then PUT the encrypted secret
   346→curl -s -X PUT \
   347→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   348→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets/API_KEY \
   349→  -d '<output from python script above>'
   350→
   351→# List secrets (names only, values hidden)
   352→curl -s \
   353→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   354→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/secrets \
   355→  | python3 -c "
   356→import sys, json
   357→for s in json.load(sys.stdin)['secrets']:
   358→    print(f\"  {s['name']:30}  updated: {s['updated_at']}\")"
   359→```
   360→
   361→Note: For secrets, `gh secret set` is dramatically simpler. If setting secrets is needed and `gh` isn't available, recommend installing it for just that operation.
   362→
   363→## 8. Releases
   364→
   365→**With gh:**
   366→
   367→```bash
   368→gh release create v1.0.0 --title "v1.0.0" --generate-notes
   369→gh release create v2.0.0-rc1 --draft --prerelease --generate-notes
   370→gh release create v1.0.0 ./dist/binary --title "v1.0.0" --notes "Release notes"
   371→gh release list
   372→gh release download v1.0.0 --dir ./downloads
   373→```
   374→
   375→**With curl:**
   376→
   377→```bash
   378→# Create a release
   379→curl -s -X POST \
   380→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   381→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases \
   382→  -d '{
   383→    "tag_name": "v1.0.0",
   384→    "name": "v1.0.0",
   385→    "body": "## Changelog\n- Feature A\n- Bug fix B",
   386→    "draft": false,
   387→    "prerelease": false,
   388→    "generate_release_notes": true
   389→  }'
   390→
   391→# List releases
   392→curl -s \
   393→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   394→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases \
   395→  | python3 -c "
   396→import sys, json
   397→for r in json.load(sys.stdin):
   398→    tag = r.get('tag_name', 'no tag')
   399→    print(f\"  {tag:15}  {r['name']:30}  {'draft' if r['draft'] else 'published'}\")"
   400→
   401→# Upload a release asset (binary file)
   402→RELEASE_ID=<id_from_create_response>
   403→curl -s -X POST \
   404→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   405→  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
   406→  "https://uploads.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases/$RELEASE_ID/assets?name=binary-amd64" \
   407→  --data-binary @./dist/binary-amd64
   408→```
   409→
   410→## 9. GitHub Actions Workflows
   411→
   412→**With gh:**
   413→
   414→```bash
   415→gh workflow list
   416→gh run list --limit 10
   417→gh run view <RUN_ID>
   418→gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
   419→gh run rerun <RUN_ID>
   420→gh run rerun <RUN_ID> --failed
   421→gh workflow run ci.yml --ref main
   422→gh workflow run deploy.yml -f environment=staging
   423→```
   424→
   425→**With curl:**
   426→
   427→```bash
   428→# List workflows
   429→curl -s \
   430→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   431→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/workflows \
   432→  | python3 -c "
   433→import sys, json
   434→for w in json.load(sys.stdin)['workflows']:
   435→    print(f\"  {w['id']:10}  {w['name']:30}  {w['state']}\")"
   436→
   437→# List recent runs

   442→import sys, json
   443→for r in json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']:
   444→    print(f\"  Run {r['id']}  {r['name']:30}  {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"
   445→
   446→# Download failed run logs
   447→RUN_ID=<run_id>
   448→curl -s -L \
   449→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   450→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
   451→  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
   452→cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs
   453→
   454→# Re-run a failed workflow
   455→curl -s -X POST \
   456→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   457→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/rerun
   458→
   459→# Re-run only failed jobs
   460→curl -s -X POST \
   461→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   462→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/rerun-failed-jobs
   463→
   464→# Trigger a workflow manually (workflow_dispatch)
   465→WORKFLOW_ID=<workflow_id_or_filename>
   466→curl -s -X POST \
   467→  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
   468→  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/workflows/$WORKFLOW_ID/dispatches \
   469→  -d '{"ref": "main", "inputs": {"environment": "staging"}}'
   470→```
   471→
   472→## 10. Gists
   473→
   474→**With gh:**
   475→

   477→gh gist create script.py --public --desc "Useful script"
   478→gh gist list
   479→```
   480→
   481→**With curl:**

   483→```bash
   484→# Create a gist

   489→    "description": "Useful script",

   496→# List your gists

   507→## Quick Reference Table

     2→name: gif-search
     3→description: Search and download GIFs from Tenor using curl. No dependencies beyond curl and jq. Useful for finding reaction GIFs, creating visual content, and sending GIFs in chat.
     4→version: 1.1.0
     5→author: Hermes Agent
     6→license: MIT
     7→prerequisites:
     8→  env_vars: [TENOR_API_KEY]
     9→  commands: [curl, jq]
    10→metadata:
    11→  hermes:
    12→    tags: [GIF, Media, Search, Tenor, API]
    13→origin:
    14→  source: hermes-agent
    15→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    16→  version: 9f22977f
    17→---
    18→
    19→# GIF Search (Tenor API)
    20→
    21→Search and download GIFs directly via the Tenor API using curl. No extra tools needed.
    22→
    23→## Setup
    24→
    25→Set your Tenor API key in your environment (add to `~/.hermes/.env`):
    26→
    27→```bash
    28→TENOR_API_KEY=your_key_here
    29→```
    30→
    31→Get a free API key at https://developers.google.com/tenor/guides/quickstart — the Google Cloud Console Tenor API key is free and has generous rate limits.
    32→
    33→## Prerequisites
    34→
    35→- `curl` and `jq` (both standard on macOS/Linux)
    36→- `TENOR_API_KEY` environment variable
    37→
    38→## Search for GIFs
    39→
    40→```bash
    41→# Search and get GIF URLs
    42→curl -s "https://tenor.googleapis.com/v2/search?q=thumbs+up&limit=5&key=${TENOR_API_KEY}" | jq -r '.results[].media_formats.gif.url'
    43→
    44→# Get smaller/preview versions
    45→curl -s "https://tenor.googleapis.com/v2/search?q=nice+work&limit=3&key=${TENOR_API_KEY}" | jq -r '.results[].media_formats.tinygif.url'
    46→```
    47→
    48→## Download a GIF
    49→
    50→```bash
    51→# Search and download the top result
    52→URL=$(curl -s "https://tenor.googleapis.com/v2/search?q=celebration&limit=1&key=${TENOR_API_KEY}" | jq -r '.results[0].media_formats.gif.url')
    53→curl -sL "$URL" -o celebration.gif
    54→```
    55→
    56→## Get Full Metadata
    57→
    58→```bash
    59→curl -s "https://tenor.googleapis.com/v2/search?q=cat&limit=3&key=${TENOR_API_KEY}" | jq '.results[] | {title: .title, url: .media_formats.gif.url, preview: .media_formats.tinygif.url, dimensions: .media_formats.gif.dims}'
    60→```
    61→
    62→## API Parameters
    63→
    64→| Parameter | Description |
    65→|-----------|-------------|
    66→| `q` | Search query (URL-encode spaces as `+`) |
    67→| `limit` | Max results (1-50, default 20) |
    68→| `key` | API key (from `$TENOR_API_KEY` env var) |
    69→| `media_filter` | Filter formats: `gif`, `tinygif`, `mp4`, `tinymp4`, `webm` |
    70→| `contentfilter` | Safety: `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high` |
    71→| `locale` | Language: `en_US`, `es`, `fr`, etc. |
    72→
    73→## Available Media Formats
    74→
    75→Each result has multiple formats under `.media_formats`:
    76→
    77→| Format | Use case |
    78→|--------|----------|
    79→| `gif` | Full quality GIF |
    80→| `tinygif` | Small preview GIF |
    81→| `mp4` | Video version (smaller file size) |
    82→| `tinymp4` | Small preview video |
    83→| `webm` | WebM video |
    84→| `nanogif` | Tiny thumbnail |
    85→
    86→## Notes
    87→
    88→- URL-encode the query: spaces as `+`, special chars as `%XX`
    89→- For sending in chat, `tinygif` URLs are lighter weight
    90→- GIF URLs can be used directly in markdown: `![alt](url)`
    91→

     2→name: heartmula
     3→description: Set up and run HeartMuLa, the open-source music generation model family (Suno-like). Generates full songs from lyrics + tags with multilingual support.
     4→version: 1.0.0
     5→metadata:
     6→  hermes:
     7→    tags: [music, audio, generation, ai, heartmula, heartcodec, lyrics, songs]
     8→    related_skills: [audiocraft]
     9→origin:
    10→  source: hermes-agent
    11→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    12→  version: 9f22977f
    13→---
    14→
    15→# HeartMuLa - Open-Source Music Generation
    16→
    17→## Overview
    18→HeartMuLa is a family of open-source music foundation models (Apache-2.0) that generates music conditioned on lyrics and tags. Comparable to Suno for open-source. Includes:
    19→- **HeartMuLa** - Music language model (3B/7B) for generation from lyrics + tags
    20→- **HeartCodec** - 12.5Hz music codec for high-fidelity audio reconstruction
    21→- **HeartTranscriptor** - Whisper-based lyrics transcription
    22→- **HeartCLAP** - Audio-text alignment model
    23→
    24→## When to Use
    25→- User wants to generate music/songs from text descriptions
    26→- User wants an open-source Suno alternative
    27→- User wants local/offline music generation
    28→- User asks about HeartMuLa, heartlib, or AI music generation
    29→
    30→## Hardware Requirements
    31→- **Minimum**: 8GB VRAM with `--lazy_load true` (loads/unloads models sequentially)
    32→- **Recommended**: 16GB+ VRAM for comfortable single-GPU usage
    33→- **Multi-GPU**: Use `--mula_device cuda:0 --codec_device cuda:1` to split across GPUs
    34→- 3B model with lazy_load peaks at ~6.2GB VRAM
    35→
    36→## Installation Steps
    37→
    38→### 1. Clone Repository
    39→```bash
    40→cd ~/  # or desired directory
    41→git clone https://github.com/HeartMuLa/heartlib.git
    42→cd heartlib
    43→```
    44→
    45→### 2. Create Virtual Environment (Python 3.10 required)
    46→```bash
    47→uv venv --python 3.10 .venv
    48→. .venv/bin/activate
    49→uv pip install -e .
    50→```
    51→
    52→### 3. Fix Dependency Compatibility Issues
    53→
    54→**IMPORTANT**: As of Feb 2026, the pinned dependencies have conflicts with newer packages. Apply these fixes:
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→# Upgrade datasets (old version incompatible with current pyarrow)
    58→uv pip install --upgrade datasets
    59→
    60→# Upgrade transformers (needed for huggingface-hub 1.x compatibility)
    61→uv pip install --upgrade transformers
    62→```
    63→
    64→### 4. Patch Source Code (Required for transformers 5.x)
    65→
    66→**Patch 1 - RoPE cache fix** in `src/heartlib/heartmula/modeling_heartmula.py`:
    67→
    68→In the `setup_caches` method of the `HeartMuLa` class, add RoPE reinitialization after the `reset_caches` try/except block and before the `with device:` block:
    69→
    70→```python
    71→# Re-initialize RoPE caches that were skipped during meta-device loading
    72→from torchtune.models.llama3_1._position_embeddings import Llama3ScaledRoPE
    73→for module in self.modules():
    74→    if isinstance(module, Llama3ScaledRoPE) and not module.is_cache_built:
    75→        module.rope_init()
    76→        module.to(device)
    77→```
    78→
    79→**Why**: `from_pretrained` creates model on meta device first; `Llama3ScaledRoPE.rope_init()` skips cache building on meta tensors, then never rebuilds after weights are loaded to real device.
    80→
    81→**Patch 2 - HeartCodec loading fix** in `src/heartlib/pipelines/music_generation.py`:
    82→
    83→Add `ignore_mismatched_sizes=True` to ALL `HeartCodec.from_pretrained()` calls (there are 2: the eager load in `__init__` and the lazy load in the `codec` property).
    84→
    85→**Why**: VQ codebook `initted` buffers have shape `[1]` in checkpoint vs `[]` in model. Same data, just scalar vs 0-d tensor. Safe to ignore.
    86→
    87→### 5. Download Model Checkpoints
    88→```bash
    89→cd heartlib  # project root
    90→hf download --local-dir './ckpt' 'HeartMuLa/HeartMuLaGen'
    91→hf download --local-dir './ckpt/HeartMuLa-oss-3B' 'HeartMuLa/HeartMuLa-oss-3B-happy-new-year'
    92→hf download --local-dir './ckpt/HeartCodec-oss' 'HeartMuLa/HeartCodec-oss-20260123'
    93→```
    94→
    95→All 3 can be downloaded in parallel. Total size is several GB.
    96→
    97→## GPU / CUDA
    98→
    99→HeartMuLa uses CUDA by default (`--mula_device cuda --codec_device cuda`). No extra setup needed if the user has an NVIDIA GPU with PyTorch CUDA support installed.
   100→
   101→- The installed `torch==2.4.1` includes CUDA 12.1 support out of the box
   102→- `torchtune` may report version `0.4.0+cpu` — this is just package metadata, it still uses CUDA via PyTorch
   103→- To verify GPU is being used, look for "CUDA memory" lines in the output (e.g. "CUDA memory before unloading: 6.20 GB")
   104→- **No GPU?** You can run on CPU with `--mula_device cpu --codec_device cpu`, but expect generation to be **extremely slow** (potentially 30-60+ minutes for a single song vs ~4 minutes on GPU). CPU mode also requires significant RAM (~12GB+ free). If the user has no NVIDIA GPU, recommend using a cloud GPU service (Google Colab free tier with T4, Lambda Labs, etc.) or the online demo at https://heartmula.github.io/ instead.
   105→
   106→## Usage
   107→
   108→### Basic Generation
   109→```bash
   110→cd heartlib
   111→. .venv/bin/activate
   112→python ./examples/run_music_generation.py \
   113→  --model_path=./ckpt \
   114→  --version="3B" \
   115→  --lyrics="./assets/lyrics.txt" \
   116→  --tags="./assets/tags.txt" \
   117→  --save_path="./assets/output.mp3" \
   118→  --lazy_load true
   119→```
   120→
   121→### Input Formatting
   122→
   123→**Tags** (comma-separated, no spaces):
   124→```
   125→piano,happy,wedding,synthesizer,romantic
   126→```
   127→or
   128→```
   129→rock,energetic,guitar,drums,male-vocal
   130→```
   131→
   132→**Lyrics** (use bracketed structural tags):
   133→```
   134→[Intro]
   135→
   136→[Verse]
   137→Your lyrics here...
   138→
   139→[Chorus]
   140→Chorus lyrics...
   141→
   142→[Bridge]
   143→Bridge lyrics...
   144→
   145→[Outro]
   146→```
   147→
   148→### Key Parameters
   149→| Parameter | Default | Description |
   150→|-----------|---------|-------------|
   151→| `--max_audio_length_ms` | 240000 | Max length in ms (240s = 4 min) |
   152→| `--topk` | 50 | Top-k sampling |
   153→| `--temperature` | 1.0 | Sampling temperature |
   154→| `--cfg_scale` | 1.5 | Classifier-free guidance scale |
   155→| `--lazy_load` | false | Load/unload models on demand (saves VRAM) |
   156→| `--mula_dtype` | bfloat16 | Dtype for HeartMuLa (bf16 recommended) |
   157→| `--codec_dtype` | float32 | Dtype for HeartCodec (fp32 recommended for quality) |
   158→
   159→### Performance
   160→- RTF (Real-Time Factor) ≈ 1.0 — a 4-minute song takes ~4 minutes to generate
   161→- Output: MP3, 48kHz stereo, 128kbps
   162→
   163→## Pitfalls
   164→1. **Do NOT use bf16 for HeartCodec** — degrades audio quality. Use fp32 (default).
   165→2. **Tags may be ignored** — known issue (#90). Lyrics tend to dominate; experiment with tag ordering.
   166→3. **Triton not available on macOS** — Linux/CUDA only for GPU acceleration.
   167→4. **RTX 5080 incompatibility** reported in upstream issues.
   168→5. The dependency pin conflicts require the manual upgrades and patches described above.
   169→
   170→## Links
   171→- Repo: https://github.com/HeartMuLa/heartlib
   172→- Models: https://huggingface.co/HeartMuLa
   173→- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10547
   174→- License: Apache-2.0
   175→

    59→| `chroma` | Pitch class distribution |
    60→| `hpss` | Harmonic/percussive separation |
    61→| `selfsim` | Self-similarity matrix |
    62→| `loudness` | Loudness over time |
    63→| `tempogram` | Tempo estimation |
    64→| `mfcc` | Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients |
    65→| `flux` | Spectral flux (onset detection) |
    66→
    67→Multiple `--viz` types render as a grid in a single image.
    68→
    69→## Common Flags
    70→
    71→| Flag | Description |
    72→|------|-------------|
    73→| `--viz` | Visualization types (comma-separated) |
    74→| `--style` | Color palette: `classic`, `magma`, `inferno`, `viridis`, `gray` |
    75→| `--width` / `--height` | Output image dimensions |
    76→| `--window` / `--hop` | FFT window and hop size |
    77→| `--min-freq` / `--max-freq` | Frequency range filter |
    78→| `--start` / `--duration` | Time slice of the audio |
    79→| `--format` | Output format: `jpg` or `png` |
    80→| `-o` | Output file path |
    81→
    82→## Notes
    83→
    84→- WAV and MP3 are decoded natively; other formats require `ffmpeg`
    85→- Output images can be inspected with `vision_analyze` for automated audio analysis
    86→- Useful for comparing audio outputs, debugging synthesis, or documenting audio processing pipelines
    87→

     2→name: youtube-content
     3→description: >
     4→  Fetch YouTube video transcripts and transform them into structured content
     5→  (chapters, summaries, threads, blog posts). Use when the user shares a YouTube
     6→  URL or video link, asks to summarize a video, requests a transcript, or wants
     7→  to extract and reformat content from any YouTube video.
     8→origin:
     9→  source: hermes-agent
    10→  url: https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent
    11→  version: 9f22977f
    12→---
    13→
    14→# YouTube Content Tool
    15→
    16→Extract transcripts from YouTube videos and convert them into useful formats.
    17→
    18→## Setup
    19→
    20→```bash
    21→pip install youtube-transcript-api
    22→```
    23→
    24→## Helper Script
    25→
    26→`SKILL_DIR` is the directory containing this SKILL.md file. The script accepts any standard YouTube URL format, short links (youtu.be), shorts, embeds, live links, or a raw 11-character video ID.
    27→
    28→```bash
    29→# JSON output with metadata
    30→python3 SKILL_DIR/scripts/fetch_transcript.py "https://youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID"
    31→
    32→# Plain text (good for piping into further processing)
    33→python3 SKILL_DIR/scripts/fetch_transcript.py "URL" --text-only
    34→
    35→# With timestamps
    36→python3 SKILL_DIR/scripts/fetch_transcript.py "URL" --timestamps
    37→
    38→# Specific language with fallback chain
    39→python3 SKILL_DIR/scripts/fetch_transcript.py "URL" --language tr,en
    40→```
    41→
    42→## Output Formats
    43→
    44→After fetching the transcript, format it based on what the user asks for:
    45→
    46→- **Chapters**: Group by topic shifts, output timestamped chapter list
    47→- **Summary**: Concise 5-10 sentence overview of the entire video
    48→- **Chapter summaries**: Chapters with a short paragraph summary for each
    49→- **Thread**: Twitter/X thread format — numbered posts, each under 280 chars
    50→- **Blog post**: Full article with title, sections, and key takeaways
    51→- **Quotes**: Notable quotes with timestamps
    52→
    53→### Example — Chapters Output
    54→
    55→```
    56→00:00 Introduction — host opens with the problem statement
    57→03:45 Background — prior work and why existing solutions fall short
    58→12:20 Core method — walkthrough of the proposed approach
    59→24:10 Results — benchmark comparisons and key takeaways
    60→31:55 Q&A — audience questions on scalability and next steps
    61→```
    62→
    63→## Workflow
    64→
    65→1. **Fetch** the transcript using the helper script with `--text-only --timestamps`.
    66→2. **Validate**: confirm the output is non-empty and in the expected language. If empty, retry without `--language` to get any available transcript. If still empty, tell the user the video likely has transcripts disabled.
    67→3. **Chunk if needed**: if the transcript exceeds ~50K characters, split into overlapping chunks (~40K with 2K overlap) and summarize each chunk before merging.
    68→4. **Transform** into the requested output format. If the user did not specify a format, default to a summary.
    69→5. **Verify**: re-read the transformed output to check for coherence, correct timestamps, and completeness before presenting.
    70→
    71→## Error Handling
    72→
    73→- **Transcript disabled**: tell the user; suggest they check if subtitles are available on the video page.
    74→- **Private/unavailable video**: relay the error and ask the user to verify the URL.
    75→- **No matching language**: retry without `--language` to fetch any available transcript, then note the actual language to the user.
    76→- **Dependency missing**: run `pip install youtube-transcript-api` and retry.
    77→

     8→metadata:
     9→  hermes:

    11→

    17→
    18→# lm-evaluation-harness - LLM Benchmarking
    19→
    20→## Quick start
    21→
    22→lm-evaluation-harness evaluates LLMs across 60+ academic benchmarks using standardized prompts and metrics.
    23→
    24→**Installation**:
    25→```bash
    26→pip install lm-eval
    27→```
    28→
    29→**Evaluate any HuggingFace model**:
    30→```bash
    31→lm_eval --model hf \
    32→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
    33→  --tasks mmlu,gsm8k,hellaswag \
    34→  --device cuda:0 \
    35→  --batch_size 8
    36→```
    37→
    38→**View available tasks**:
    39→```bash
    40→lm_eval --tasks list
    41→```
    42→
    43→## Common workflows
    44→
    45→### Workflow 1: Standard benchmark evaluation
    46→
    47→Evaluate model on core benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval).
    48→
    49→Copy this checklist:
    50→
    51→```
    52→Benchmark Evaluation:
    53→- [ ] Step 1: Choose benchmark suite
    54→- [ ] Step 2: Configure model
    55→- [ ] Step 3: Run evaluation
    56→- [ ] Step 4: Analyze results
    57→```
    58→
    59→**Step 1: Choose benchmark suite**
    60→
    61→**Core reasoning benchmarks**:
    62→- **MMLU** (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) - 57 subjects, multiple choice
    63→- **GSM8K** - Grade school math word problems
    64→- **HellaSwag** - Common sense reasoning
    65→- **TruthfulQA** - Truthfulness and factuality
    66→- **ARC** (AI2 Reasoning Challenge) - Science questions
    67→
    68→**Code benchmarks**:
    69→- **HumanEval** - Python code generation (164 problems)
    70→- **MBPP** (Mostly Basic Python Problems) - Python coding
    71→
    72→**Standard suite** (recommended for model releases):
    73→```bash
    74→--tasks mmlu,gsm8k,hellaswag,truthfulqa,arc_challenge
    75→```
    76→
    77→**Step 2: Configure model**
    78→
    79→**HuggingFace model**:
    80→```bash
    81→lm_eval --model hf \
    82→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf,dtype=bfloat16 \
    83→  --tasks mmlu \
    84→  --device cuda:0 \
    85→  --batch_size auto  # Auto-detect optimal batch size
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Quantized model (4-bit/8-bit)**:
    89→```bash
    90→lm_eval --model hf \
    91→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf,load_in_4bit=True \
    92→  --tasks mmlu \
    93→  --device cuda:0
    94→```
    95→
    96→**Custom checkpoint**:
    97→```bash
    98→lm_eval --model hf \
    99→  --model_args pretrained=/path/to/my-model,tokenizer=/path/to/tokenizer \
   100→  --tasks mmlu \
   101→  --device cuda:0
   102→```
   103→
   104→**Step 3: Run evaluation**
   105→
   106→```bash
   107→# Full MMLU evaluation (57 subjects)
   108→lm_eval --model hf \
   109→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
   110→  --tasks mmlu \
   111→  --num_fewshot 5 \  # 5-shot evaluation (standard)
   112→  --batch_size 8 \
   113→  --output_path results/ \
   114→  --log_samples  # Save individual predictions
   115→
   116→# Multiple benchmarks at once
   117→lm_eval --model hf \
   118→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
   119→  --tasks mmlu,gsm8k,hellaswag,truthfulqa,arc_challenge \
   120→  --num_fewshot 5 \
   121→  --batch_size 8 \
   122→  --output_path results/llama2-7b-eval.json
   123→```
   124→
   125→**Step 4: Analyze results**
   126→
   127→Results saved to `results/llama2-7b-eval.json`:
   128→
   129→```json
   130→{
   131→  "results": {
   132→    "mmlu": {
   133→      "acc": 0.459,
   134→      "acc_stderr": 0.004
   135→    },
   136→    "gsm8k": {
   137→      "exact_match": 0.142,
   138→      "exact_match_stderr": 0.006
   139→    },
   140→    "hellaswag": {
   141→      "acc_norm": 0.765,
   142→      "acc_norm_stderr": 0.004
   143→    }
   144→  },
   145→  "config": {
   146→    "model": "hf",
   147→    "model_args": "pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf",
   148→    "num_fewshot": 5
   149→  }
   150→}
   151→```
   152→
   153→### Workflow 2: Track training progress
   154→
   155→Evaluate checkpoints during training.
   156→
   157→```
   158→Training Progress Tracking:
   159→- [ ] Step 1: Set up periodic evaluation
   160→- [ ] Step 2: Choose quick benchmarks
   161→- [ ] Step 3: Automate evaluation
   162→- [ ] Step 4: Plot learning curves
   163→```
   164→
   165→**Step 1: Set up periodic evaluation**
   166→
   167→Evaluate every N training steps:
   168→
   169→```bash
   170→#!/bin/bash
   171→# eval_checkpoint.sh
   172→
   173→CHECKPOINT_DIR=$1
   174→STEP=$2
   175→
   176→lm_eval --model hf \
   177→  --model_args pretrained=$CHECKPOINT_DIR/checkpoint-$STEP \
   178→  --tasks gsm8k,hellaswag \
   179→  --num_fewshot 0 \  # 0-shot for speed
   180→  --batch_size 16 \
   181→  --output_path results/step-$STEP.json
   182→```
   183→
   184→**Step 2: Choose quick benchmarks**
   185→
   186→Fast benchmarks for frequent evaluation:
   187→- **HellaSwag**: ~10 minutes on 1 GPU
   188→- **GSM8K**: ~5 minutes
   189→- **PIQA**: ~2 minutes
   190→
   191→Avoid for frequent eval (too slow):
   192→- **MMLU**: ~2 hours (57 subjects)
   193→- **HumanEval**: Requires code execution
   194→
   195→**Step 3: Automate evaluation**
   196→
   197→Integrate with training script:
   198→
   199→```python
   200→# In training loop
   201→if step % eval_interval == 0:
   202→    model.save_pretrained(f"checkpoints/step-{step}")
   203→
   204→    # Run evaluation
   205→    os.system(f"./eval_checkpoint.sh checkpoints step-{step}")
   206→```
   207→
   208→Or use PyTorch Lightning callbacks:
   209→
   210→```python
   211→from pytorch_lightning import Callback
   212→
   213→class EvalHarnessCallback(Callback):
   214→    def on_validation_epoch_end(self, trainer, pl_module):
   215→        step = trainer.global_step
   216→        checkpoint_path = f"checkpoints/step-{step}"
   217→
   218→        # Save checkpoint
   219→        trainer.save_checkpoint(checkpoint_path)
   220→
   221→        # Run lm-eval
   222→        os.system(f"lm_eval --model hf --model_args pretrained={checkpoint_path} ...")
   223→```
   224→
   225→**Step 4: Plot learning curves**
   226→
   227→```python
   228→import json
   229→import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
   230→
   231→# Load all results
   232→steps = []
   233→mmlu_scores = []
   234→
   235→for file in sorted(glob.glob("results/step-*.json")):
   236→    with open(file) as f:
   237→        data = json.load(f)
   238→        step = int(file.split("-")[1].split(".")[0])
   239→        steps.append(step)
   240→        mmlu_scores.append(data["results"]["mmlu"]["acc"])
   241→
   242→# Plot
   243→plt.plot(steps, mmlu_scores)
   244→plt.xlabel("Training Step")
   245→plt.ylabel("MMLU Accuracy")
   246→plt.title("Training Progress")
   247→plt.savefig("training_curve.png")
   248→```
   249→
   250→### Workflow 3: Compare multiple models
   251→
   252→Benchmark suite for model comparison.
   253→
   254→```
   255→Model Comparison:
   256→- [ ] Step 1: Define model list
   257→- [ ] Step 2: Run evaluations
   258→- [ ] Step 3: Generate comparison table
   259→```
   260→
   261→**Step 1: Define model list**
   262→
   263→```bash
   264→# models.txt
   265→meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf
   266→meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf
   267→mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1
   268→microsoft/phi-2
   269→```
   270→
   271→**Step 2: Run evaluations**
   272→
   273→```bash
   274→#!/bin/bash
   275→# eval_all_models.sh
   276→
   277→TASKS="mmlu,gsm8k,hellaswag,truthfulqa"
   278→
   279→while read model; do
   280→    echo "Evaluating $model"
   281→
   282→    # Extract model name for output file
   283→    model_name=$(echo $model | sed 's/\//-/g')
   284→
   285→    lm_eval --model hf \
   286→      --model_args pretrained=$model,dtype=bfloat16 \
   287→      --tasks $TASKS \
   288→      --num_fewshot 5 \
   289→      --batch_size auto \
   290→      --output_path results/$model_name.json
   291→
   292→done < models.txt
   293→```
   294→
   295→**Step 3: Generate comparison table**
   296→
   297→```python
   298→import json
   299→import pandas as pd
   300→
   301→models = [
   302→    "meta-llama-Llama-2-7b-hf",
   303→    "meta-llama-Llama-2-13b-hf",
   304→    "mistralai-Mistral-7B-v0.1",
   305→    "microsoft-phi-2"
   306→]
   307→
   308→tasks = ["mmlu", "gsm8k", "hellaswag", "truthfulqa"]
   309→
   310→results = []
   311→for model in models:
   312→    with open(f"results/{model}.json") as f:
   313→        data = json.load(f)
   314→        row = {"Model": model.replace("-", "/")}
   315→        for task in tasks:
   316→            # Get primary metric for each task
   317→            metrics = data["results"][task]
   318→            if "acc" in metrics:
   319→                row[task.upper()] = f"{metrics['acc']:.3f}"
   320→            elif "exact_match" in metrics:
   321→                row[task.upper()] = f"{metrics['exact_match']:.3f}"
   322→        results.append(row)
   323→
   324→df = pd.DataFrame(results)
   325→print(df.to_markdown(index=False))
   326→```
   327→
   328→Output:
   329→```
   330→| Model                  | MMLU  | GSM8K | HELLASWAG | TRUTHFULQA |
   331→|------------------------|-------|-------|-----------|------------|
   332→| meta-llama/Llama-2-7b  | 0.459 | 0.142 | 0.765     | 0.391      |
   333→| meta-llama/Llama-2-13b | 0.549 | 0.287 | 0.801     | 0.430      |
   334→| mistralai/Mistral-7B   | 0.626 | 0.395 | 0.812     | 0.428      |
   335→| microsoft/phi-2        | 0.560 | 0.613 | 0.682     | 0.447      |
   336→```
   337→
   338→### Workflow 4: Evaluate with vLLM (faster inference)
   339→
   340→Use vLLM backend for 5-10x faster evaluation.
   341→
   342→```
   343→vLLM Evaluation:
   344→- [ ] Step 1: Install vLLM
   345→- [ ] Step 2: Configure vLLM backend
   346→- [ ] Step 3: Run evaluation
   347→```
   348→
   349→**Step 1: Install vLLM**
   350→
   351→```bash
   352→pip install vllm
   353→```
   354→
   355→**Step 2: Configure vLLM backend**
   356→
   357→```bash
   358→lm_eval --model vllm \
   359→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf,tensor_parallel_size=1,dtype=auto,gpu_memory_utilization=0.8 \
   360→  --tasks mmlu \
   361→  --batch_size auto
   362→```
   363→
   364→**Step 3: Run evaluation**
   365→
   366→vLLM is 5-10× faster than standard HuggingFace:
   367→
   368→```bash
   369→# Standard HF: ~2 hours for MMLU on 7B model
   370→lm_eval --model hf \
   371→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf \
   372→  --tasks mmlu \
   373→  --batch_size 8
   374→
   375→# vLLM: ~15-20 minutes for MMLU on 7B model
   376→lm_eval --model vllm \
   377→  --model_args pretrained=meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf,tensor_parallel_size=2 \
   378→  --tasks mmlu \
   379→  --batch_size auto
   380→```
   381→
   382→## When to use vs alternatives
   383→
   384→**Use lm-evaluation-harness when:**
   385→- Benchmarking models for academic papers
   386→- Comparing model quality across standard tasks
   387→- Tracking training progress
   388→- Reporting standardized metrics (everyone uses same prompts)
   389→- Need reproducible evaluation
   390→
   391→**Use alternatives instead:**
   392→- **HELM** (Stanford): Broader evaluation (fairness, efficiency, calibration)
   393→- **AlpacaEval**: Instruction-following evaluation with LLM judges
   394→- **MT-Bench**: Conversational multi-turn evaluation
   395→- **Custom scripts**: Domain-specific evaluation
   396→
   397→## Common issues
   398→
   399→**Issue: Evaluation too slow**
   400→
   401→Use vLLM backend:
   402→```bash
   403→lm_eval --model vllm \
   404→  --model_args pretrained=model-name,tensor_parallel_size=2
   405→```
   406→
   407→Or reduce fewshot examples:
   408→```bash
   409→--num_fewshot 0  # Instead of 5
   410→```
   411→
   412→Or evaluate subset of MMLU:
   413→```bash
   414→--tasks mmlu_stem  # Only STEM subjects
   415→```
   416→
   417→**Issue: Out of memory**
   418→
   419→Reduce batch size:
   420→```bash
   421→--batch_size 1  # Or --batch_size auto
   422→```
   423→
   424→Use quantization:
   425→```bash
   426→--model_args pretrained=model-name,load_in_8bit=True
   427→```
   428→
   429→Enable CPU offloading:
   430→```bash
   431→--model_args pretrained=model-name,device_map=auto,offload_folder=offload
   432→```
   433→
   434→**Issue: Different results than reported**
   435→
   436→Check fewshot count:
   437→```bash
   438→--num_fewshot 5  # Most papers use 5-shot
   439→```
   440→
   441→Check exact task name:
   442→```bash
   443→--tasks mmlu  # Not mmlu_direct or mmlu_fewshot
   444→```
   445→
   446→Verify model and tokenizer match:
   447→```bash
   448→--model_args pretrained=model-name,tokenizer=same-model-name
   449→```
   450→
   451→**Issue: HumanEval not executing code**
   452→
   453→Install execution dependencies:
   454→```bash
   455→pip install human-eval
   456→```
   457→
   458→Enable code execution:
   459→```bash
   460→lm_eval --model hf \
   461→  --model_args pretrained=model-name \
   462→  --tasks humaneval \
   463→  --allow_code_execution  # Required for HumanEval
   464→```
   465→
   466→## Advanced topics
   467→
   468→**Benchmark descriptions**: See [references/benchmark-guide.md](references/benchmark-guide.md) for detailed description of all 60+ tasks, what they measure, and interpretation.
   469→
   470→**Custom tasks**: See [references/custom-tasks.md](references/custom-tasks.md) for creating domain-specific evaluation tasks.
   471→
   472→**API evaluation**: See [references/api-evaluation.md](references/api-evaluation.md) for evaluating OpenAI, Anthropic, and other API models.
   473→
   474→**Multi-GPU strategies**: See [references/distributed-eval.md](references/distributed-eval.md) for data parallel and tensor parallel evaluation.
   475→
   476→## Hardware requirements
   477→
   478→- **GPU**: NVIDIA (CUDA 11.8+), works on CPU (very slow)
   479→- **VRAM**:
   480→  - 7B model: 16GB (bf16) or 8GB (8-bit)
   481→  - 13B model: 28GB (bf16) or 14GB (8-bit)
   482→  - 70B model: Requires multi-GPU or quantization
   483→- **Time** (7B model, single A100):
   484→  - HellaSwag: 10 minutes
   485→  - GSM8K: 5 minutes
   486→  - MMLU (full): 2 hours
   487→  - HumanEval: 20 minutes

   494→- Leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/HuggingFaceH4/open_llm_leaderboard (uses this harness)
